Sydney.Spring/Summer 2027: May 11–15, 2026 (Australian Fashion Week, covering Resort 2027 and Spring 2027)

shows.bio: Founded in 1946 by Christian Dior; the 1947 “New Look” reshaped postwar fashion and still anchors the house's silhouette today. Jonathan Anderson became sole creative director in 2025, the first person to oversee womenswear, menswear, and couture together.

shows.playlist: Lady Gaga's “Just Dance” (remixed), with a Billy Elliot voiceover and a Pride & Prejudice score cue
shows.bio: French couture house founded in 1910 by Gabrielle “Coco” Chanel; built its identity on tweed suiting, the little black dress, and No. 5. Matthieu Blazy has been creative director since 2025, arriving from Bottega Veneta.
Founded in 1961 by Yves Saint Laurent and Pierre Bergé; credited with bringing the tuxedo (Le Smoking) into womenswear. Anthony Vaccarello has been creative director since 2016.

Founded in 2001 by Stella McCartney in London; the house has been leather- and fur-free from day one and has since developed plant-based faux fur and lab-grown vegan silk. McCartney remains creative director of her own label.

Spanish leather goods house dating to 1846 in Madrid, among the oldest names on any fashion week calendar. Jack McCollough and Lazaro Hernandez, the founders of Proenza Schouler, became co-creative directors in 2025.

Founded in 1952 by Hubert de Givenchy, closely associated with Audrey Hepburn's screen wardrobe in the 1950s and '60s. Sarah Burton has been creative director since 2024, following two decades at Alexander McQueen.
Founded in 1969 by Rei Kawakubo in Tokyo, long associated with deconstruction and challenging conventional ideas of beauty. Kawakubo remains creative director of her own label.

Founded in 2012 by Virgil Abloh in Milan, credited with helping bring streetwear into the luxury runway conversation. Abloh died in 2021; the brand has since been without a permanent creative director following Ib Kamara's departure.

shows.debut: Maria Grazia Chiuri's debut as creative director
shows.bio: Founded in 1925 by Adele and Edoardo Fendi in Rome, starting as a fur and leather workshop. Maria Grazia Chiuri became creative director in 2026, arriving from Dior.

shows.debut: Meryll Rogge's debut as creative director
shows.bio: Founded in 1994 by Consuelo Castiglioni in Milan, known for offbeat prints and asymmetric silhouettes. Meryll Rogge became creative director in 2026, following her own eponymous label.

shows.debut: Demna's runway debut as creative director
shows.stylist: Styled in-house by Demna — no separate stylist credited
shows.bio: Founded in 1921 by Guccio Gucci in Florence, originally producing leather luggage. Demna became creative director in 2025, arriving from Balenciaga.

shows.venue: A palazzo near La Scala, Milan
shows.bio: Founded in 1966 in Vicenza, Italy; best known for its intrecciato woven leather technique. Louise Trotter has been creative director since 2025, arriving from Carven.

shows.playlist: A 90s rave-leaning set — D-Shake, Dustin Zahn, and Robert Hood among the tracks, growing more erratic as the show went on
shows.bio: Founded in 1913 by Mario Prada in Milan as a leather goods shop; became a fashion house under Miuccia Prada from the 1980s on. Miuccia Prada and Raf Simons have served as co-creative directors since 2020.

shows.debut: Loris Messina and Simone Rizzo's debut as co-creative directors
shows.bio: Founded in 1983 by Franco Moschino in Milan, built on a tradition of pointed, satirical takes on fashion itself. Loris Messina and Simone Rizzo, formerly of Sunnei, were named co-creative directors in 2026.

Founded in 1913 by Mario Prada in Milan as a leather goods shop; became a fashion house under Miuccia Prada from the 1980s on. Miuccia Prada and Raf Simons have served as co-creative directors since 2020.

Founded in 2013 by Dhruv Kapoor in Milan after he moved from New Delhi to study at Istituto Marangoni, known for gender-fluid ready-to-wear blending Indian craftsmanship, fine embroidery and bold color with streetwear-inflected silhouettes. Kapoor previously worked at Etro, won the Vogue India Fashion Fund in 2015, and the label opened a Delhi flagship store in 2026.

Founded in 1978 by Renzo Rosso as an alternative to casual denim brands of the era. Belgian designer Glenn Martens has been artistic director since 2020, known for reviving the brand through viral, boundary-pushing denim.

J.Salinas is the eponymous label of Peruvian designer Jorge Luis Salinas, known for merging Andean cultural heritage with contemporary design through handmade garments crafted with Peruvian women artisans. The brand's signature is couture-level crochet and layered textile work in native Peruvian fibers such as alpaca and Pima cotton. Salinas, a Philadelphia College of Textiles and Science graduate, has shown at Milan Fashion Week for five editions and won Artisanal Project of the Year at the 2025 Latin American Fashion Awards.

shows.debut: Vivetta Ponti’s fresh start after 18 years, launching on Milan Fashion Week’s opening day
shows.bio: A brand-new label from designer Vivetta Ponti, who exited her original namesake company Vivetta after 18 years to launch Venerdì Pomeriggio (“Friday Afternoon”) — keeping her signature girly, whimsical aesthetic but built around smaller production, sustainability, and lower price points.

Founded in 1979 by Luisa Beccaria in Milan, known for romantic, ultra-feminine dresses with ruffles, florals and luxurious fabrics. Her eldest daughter Lucilla Bonaccorsi joined the brand's artistic direction in 2009. The house's gowns have been worn by celebrities including Halle Berry, Charlize Theron, Uma Thurman and Nicole Kidman.
Founded in 1968 in Hamburg by Jil Sander, known for minimalist, clean tailoring; acquired by Prada in 1999 and later by OTB Group in 2021. Simone Bellotti has served as creative director.

Founded in 1997 by Daniela Gregis in Bergamo, known for artisanal, handmade garments in natural fabrics (cotton, linen, hemp, silk) with layered, deconstructed silhouettes, relaxed shapes and occasional hand-painted motifs. Gregis initially trained as a herbalist before entering fashion; her daughter Marta Bortolotti has taken on a leadership role and signed the SS27 'Ambra' show.

shows.venue: Via Cola Di Rienzo angolo Via Moisè Loria, Milan
shows.bio: Sardinian designer Antonio Marras launched his brand in 1987, later serving as artistic director of Kenzo from 2003 to 2011. Calzedonia acquired an 80% stake in 2023, with Marras remaining creative director.
Founded in 1925 by Adele and Edoardo Fendi in Rome, starting as a fur and leather workshop. Maria Grazia Chiuri became creative director in 2026, arriving from Dior.

Founded in 2008 by Vivetta Ponti in Italy, known for whimsical, fairy-tale womenswear with trompe-l'oeil prints, surreal details and baby-doll silhouettes. Founder Ponti departed in 2026 to launch Venerdì Pomeriggio; the brand is now owned by the Anselmi family (Modamet) with CEO Nicoletta Raponi.
shows.cd: In-house design team (founder Vivetta Ponti departed 2026)

shows.venue: Via Dei Cavalieri Del Santo Sepolcro, Milan
shows.bio: Founded in 1953 in Gallarate by Ottavio and Rosita Missoni, known for colorful zigzag-patterned knitwear. Family-run for three generations; Alberto Caliri is creative director, with Angela Missoni as president. Rosita Missoni passed away in late 2025 at age 93.

Launched in 1997 as “Line 6” within Martin Margiela’s numbered house structure — a more casual, street-inspired counterpart to the main Maison Margiela line. True to Margiela’s ethos, MM6’s collections are directed by an anonymous studio collective rather than a named designer.
Founded by Gimmo Etro, known for its signature paisley print. A family business: children Kean, Veronica, and Jacopo Etro have led menswear, womenswear, and accessories respectively.
shows.cd: In-house design team (after Marco De Vincenzo's 2026 exit)

shows.bio: Japanese sports-shoe brand founded in 1949 in Kobe by Kihachiro Onitsuka, later merging into ASICS in 1977. Revived as a standalone fashion label in Europe in 2002, best known for the Mexico 66 sneaker.

Founded in 1951 in Reggio Emilia by Achille Maramotti, still family-owned. Rather than a single creative director, design is led by a longtime studio team under design director Laura Lusuardi, with chairman Luigi Maramotti.
Founded in 1962 in Ancona by Arnaldo Girombelli, named for his eldest daughter. Sara Cavazza Facchini is creative director.

Founded in 2022 by Phan Dang Hoang in Milan, known for translating Vietnamese artistic heritage, traditional materials and crafts — including lacquer-inspired layering and references to silk painting and ceramics — into contemporary silhouettes. The designer was named to the Forbes 30 Under 30 Asia (Arts) list in 2024.

Founded in 1993 in Milan by Japanese designer Izumi Ogino, who joined Milano Moda Donna in 1998 as the first Japanese woman to do so. Known for soft knitwear and the hand-knit WIREBAG, introduced in 1998.
Founded in 1994 by Consuelo Castiglioni in Milan, known for offbeat prints and asymmetric silhouettes. Meryll Rogge became creative director in 2026, following her own eponymous label.

Italian designer Francesco Murano (b. 1997, Agropoli), founder of his namesake womenswear brand, launched in 2021 after studying fashion in Milan. An LVMH Prize finalist who has dressed Beyoncé, Katy Perry, Gisele Bündchen, and Zendaya. Debuted on the official Milan Fashion Week calendar in February 2025.

Founded in 1981 by Alberta Ferretti in Milan, known for ethereal, romantic silhouettes in soft, draped fabrics. Ferretti designed the collection herself through 2024; the brand is part of the Aeffe group, which she co-founded with her brother Massimo.
Founded in 1970 by Roberto Cavalli, known for animal prints and maximalist glamour. Cavalli died in April 2024 at age 83; Fausto Puglisi is creative director. Acquired by Marquee Brands in May 2026.

Circular, genderless, solarpunk ready-to-wear brand founded in 2021 by Flora Rabitti, based between Mantua and Milan. Artisanal, made-to-order production using upcycling, textile manipulation and natural dyeing; on the official Milan Fashion Week calendar since 2022. Winner of the 2023 CNMI Fashion Trust prize (Max&Co. 'Design for Change' award). Rabitti studied at IED Milan, worked for Miu Miu, trained at Institut Français de la Couture (Paris) and Central Saint Martins (London).

Roots trace to a shoemaking workshop founded by Filippo Della Valle in the early 1900s in the Marche region; his grandson Diego Della Valle built it into the global Tod’s brand, best known for the hand-stitched, rubber-studded Gommino driving shoe.

A Milan-based project founded in 2024 by Galib Gassanoff — born in Georgia and raised in an Azerbaijani community — using fashion, textile research, and craft to preserve Caucasus heritage. Gassanoff previously co-founded the label Act N°1 before leaving in 2023 to build Institution as a cultural project rather than a conventional brand.

Launched in 1969 by Achille Maramotti as a more experimental, avant-garde offshoot of Max Mara, focused on precision tailoring and material research. Creative direction is currently led by Grazia Malagoli.
Italian label built around a romantic, rose-strewn femininity by Anna Molinari, nicknamed the “queen of roses.” A family business: her daughter Rossella also designs for the house.
Founded in 1921 by Guccio Gucci in Florence, originally producing leather luggage. Demna became creative director in 2025, arriving from Balenciaga.

Founded in Milan by Simone Cracker (b. 1985), who began in 2006 making accessories from upholstery materials before officially launching Simon Cracker in 2010. Built entirely on giving old and unused clothes and materials new life through patchwork and upcycling.

Self-made Bologna designer Elisabetta Franchi founded Betty Blue S.p.A. in 1998, renaming the brand after herself in 2012. Known for figure-flattering, accessible-luxury womenswear; the brand went fur-free in 2012-2013 and later eliminated down and angora wool.

Founded in 1928 in Perugia by Luisa Spagnoli, who revolutionized Italian knitwear with angora wool (and separately invented the Bacio Perugina chocolate). Now led by her descendant Nicoletta Spagnoli.

Founded in 2016 by Gilda Ambrosio and Giorgia Tordini, capturing the glamour of nocturnal Milan through shimmering fabrics and body-conscious silhouettes. This season marks the brand’s 10th anniversary.

Founded by Mexican-Ecuadorian designer Neithan Herbert Ruiz Pillajo, a 2020 IED Milan graduate who debuted through Milano Moda Graduate, known for romantic, artisanal and sustainability-minded collections drawing on Indigenous Ecuadorian and Mexican heritage and collaborations with artisans. He is making his Milan Fashion Week debut with the Spring/Summer 2027 collection.
Founded in 2000 in Florence by designer Ermanno Scervino and entrepreneur Toni Scervino, blending sportswear ease with couture-level Florentine craftsmanship.

Founded in 1927 by Salvatore Ferragamo, the shoemaker to Hollywood’s golden age. Maximilian Davis has been creative director since 2022, bringing a contemporary, playful edge while staying rooted in the house’s codes.

Founded in 1985 in Legnano by Domenico Dolce and Stefano Gabbana, epitomizing Italian glamour and sensuality. Gabbana stepped down as chairman in late 2025 but remains co-creative director alongside Dolce.

Founded in 2009 in Milan by Massimo Giorgetti, blending traditional Italian tailoring with youthful, Technicolor sportswear codes. Giorgetti also served as creative director of Emilio Pucci from 2015-2017.

Founded in 1972 by Laura Biagiotti, nicknamed the “Queen of Cashmere” by the New York Times. Biagiotti died in 2017; the house is now led by her daughter, Lavinia Biagiotti Cigna, the third generation of an all-female design dynasty.

Founded in 2016 in Reggio Emilia by Luca Lin and Galib Gassanoff, known for tailoring fused with dramatic tulle ruffles and hybrid, deconstructed garments mixing multicultural craft references. Won the 2017 'Who Is On Next?' emerging-talent prize (AltaRoma/Vogue Italia); Gassanoff departed in early 2023, leaving Luca Lin as sole creative director, and the label has been worn by Beyoncé, Lady Gaga, Lizzo and Dua Lipa.

Bologna-born designer Marco Rambaldi founded his label built on inclusivity, upcycling, and a gender-fluid aesthetic, drawing on 1970s Italy. A CNMI Fashion Trust Grant finalist, championed early by Pierpaolo Piccioli.

Founded in 2022 by Ghanaian-born designer Victor Reginald Bob Abbey-Hart in Milan, known for architectural denim tailoring fusing military and workwear influences with Made-in-Italy craftsmanship. Debuted at Milan Fashion Week Men's in 2026 with the 'Anatomy of Void' collection.
Founded in 1966 in Vicenza, Italy; best known for its intrecciato woven leather technique. Louise Trotter has been creative director since 2025, arriving from Carven.
Founded in 1998 by German designer and entrepreneur Philipp Plein, known for maximalist, rhinestone-heavy luxury streetwear. Headquartered in Lugano, Switzerland.

Founded in 2007 by Zhao Huizhou in Shenzhen, HUI is a Chinese luxury womenswear brand known for translating Chinese intangible cultural heritage — Miao embroidery, silver ornamentation and silk artistry — into contemporary designs that fuse Eastern aesthetics with Western tailoring. Zhao, who holds a master's degree from the Politecnico di Milano, also established the HUI Foundation in 2016 to preserve traditional Chinese crafts, and in 2025 she became the first Chinese designer to receive the TaoModa Tao Award.

Founded in 1975 by Giorgio Armani, who redefined masculine and feminine elegance through deconstructed, minimalist tailoring. Armani passed away in September 2025 at age 91; his niece Silvana Armani, already his longtime design deputy, now leads ready-to-wear.

shows.debut: First season on the official Milan Fashion Week calendar
shows.bio: Founded in 2011 in London by Portuguese designers Marta Marques and Paulo Almeida, both Central Saint Martins graduates. Credited with helping launch the 2010s revival of distressed, reworked denim; winners of the LVMH Prize.

Founded in 2017 by Mattia Piazza in Palermo, known for sartorial tailoring with clerical-inspired lines rooted in the brand's 'buono uguale bello' (good equals beautiful) philosophy and slow, ethical, locally produced craftsmanship. The brand takes its name from the baroque painter Mattia Preti and frequently uses its collections as platforms for social and political commentary; Piazza studied music before moving into fashion design.

Founded in 2021 by Rainy Womack in Los Angeles, known for luxury streetwear blending raw emotion with handmade Italian craftsmanship. Went viral after its Paris Bag appeared on Netflix's Selling Sunset; debuted on the official Milan Fashion Week calendar in 2026.

Womenswear label founded in 2009 by Rome-born designer Francesca Liberatore (b. 1983) after winning the Camera Nazionale della Moda Italiana's Next Generation competition; she graduated from Central Saint Martins in 2007 and previously worked with Viktor&Rolf, Jean Paul Gaultier and Brioni Womenswear.

Founded in 1988 by Portuguese designer Miguel Vieira, known for refined tailoring and luxurious eveningwear in silk and satin with a sophisticated, modern sensibility. A longtime fixture of Portugal Fashion, he has shown internationally from São Paulo to Milan.

Founded in 2019 by Luke Radloff in Johannesburg, known for sustainable, timeless tailoring in natural fibers with a muted palette and modular, trans-seasonal pieces. Radloff was the inaugural winner of the Azzedine Alaïa Foundation x Orveda Prize in 2023.

Founded in 2008 by Nadya Dzyak in Dnipro, Ukraine, known for architectural forms, feminine silhouettes, and sculptural hand-laid pleats and ruffles in translucent fabrics. The brand donates 20% of all orders to the Ukrainian army.

London-based label by Central Saint Martins menswear graduate Timisola Shasanya, known for intricate textiles and sculptural menswear exploring migration, race and identity between Nigeria and the UK. A Sarabande Foundation scholar who interned with JW Anderson, Ferragamo and Jawara Alleyne.

Founded in 2021 by Ethiopian designer Mastewal Alemu in Addis Ababa, known for high-end womenswear crafted from handwoven 100% cotton made on traditional looms by local artisans. The brand champions sustainability and a zero-waste design approach, and was highlighted by Vogue Italy as a brand to watch in Ethiopia.
Founded in 2007 by Babatunde 'Papa' Oyeyemi in Lagos, known for gender-fluid, androgynous fashion rooted in Nigerian menswear traditions. The brand debuted at Milan Women's Fashion Week in 2021.

Founded in 2011 in London by Nigerian-British textile designer Banke Kuku, known for vibrant African-inspired printed textiles in bold colour and luxury occasion loungewear, with fabrics also produced for the interiors industry. The founder trained in textile design at Central Saint Martins and Chelsea College of Art, and her designs have been worn by Gabrielle Union, Lupita Nyong'o, Naomi Campbell and Beyoncé.

Founded in 2000 by German designer Kathrin von Rechenberg in Beijing, known for made-to-measure couture in Xiang Yun Sha (tea silk) with clean geometric, architectural forms blending German precision, French couture craft and Chinese influence. Kathrin trained at the Ecole de la Chambre Syndicale de la Couture Parisienne and previously worked at Dior and Chanel.

Founded in 1856 by Thomas Burberry in Basingstoke, England; invented gabardine and popularized the trench coat. Daniel Lee has been creative director since 2022. ReBurberry Services offers repair, reproofing, and restoration for existing pieces.
Founded in 2005 by Erdem Moralioğlu in London, known for painterly florals and literary, historical references. Moralioğlu remains creative director of his own label.
Founded in 2010 by Simone Rocha in London, known for pairing romantic, feminine fabrics with harder, more confrontational details. Rocha remains creative director of her own label.
London-based designer known for “reformative luxury” built on deadstock fabric, upcycled denim, and leather. Coker remains creative director of her own label.

Founded by Emma Chopova and Laura Lowena in London, known for kilts and pieces built from recycled materials and deadstock textiles like pillowcases and aprons. Chopova and Lowena remain co-creative directors of their own label.
American designer based between London and New York, known for upcycling deadstock fabric and secondhand garments into new pieces. Ives remains creative director of his own label.
Founded in 2016 by Catherine Holstein in New York, known for elevated, quietly sexy basics. Holstein remains creative director of her own label.

shows.debut: Rachel Scott's debut with full creative control
shows.bio: Founded in 2002 by Jack McCollough and Lazaro Hernandez, then Parsons classmates, in New York. Rachel Scott became creative director in 2026 after the founders' move to Loewe.

shows.venue: Sotheby's (Marcel Breuer building), Madison Avenue, New York
shows.bio: Founded in 2004 by Tory Burch in New York, built around a preppy-with-an-edge American style. Burch remains creative director of her own label.

American leather goods house founded in 1941 in New York; Stuart Vevers has been creative director since 2013, leaning the house into youthful, downtown Americana. Its (Re)Loved program repairs, restores, and buys back used Coach pieces for resale.

Founded in 2011 by Mike Eckhaus and Zoe Latta in Los Angeles, now showing in New York; known for raw, unfinished-looking construction and a longstanding pre-loved runway partnership with eBay. Eckhaus and Latta remain co-creative directors of their own label.
American designer who launched his eponymous label in the 1980s; credited with bringing grunge to the runway in 1992. Jacobs remains creative director of his own label.
Founded by Elsa Schiaparelli in 1927, revived in 2012 and now led by Daniel Roseberry, known for surrealist, body-as-object couture. Traditionally opens the official Haute Couture calendar.

Founded in 1946 by Christian Dior; the 1947 “New Look” reshaped postwar fashion and still anchors the house's silhouette today. Jonathan Anderson became sole creative director in 2025, the first person to oversee womenswear, menswear, and couture together.

French couture house founded in 1910 by Gabrielle “Coco” Chanel; built its identity on tweed suiting, the little black dress, and No. 5. Matthieu Blazy has been creative director since 2025, arriving from Bottega Veneta.

Founded in 1919 by Cristóbal Balenciaga in San Sebastián before relocating to Paris; long regarded as a technician's house for its sculptural tailoring. Pierpaolo Piccioli became creative director in 2025, arriving from Valentino.

Founded by Jean Paul Gaultier in 1976. After years of rotating guest designers presenting couture under his name, Duran Lantink was named permanent creative director in 2026 to carry the house's sculptural, boundary-pushing legacy forward.
Giorgio Armani's couture line, launched in 2005. Following Giorgio Armani's death, Silvana Armani has led creative direction of the house.
Founded by Lebanese designer Elie Saab in 1982, a couture mainstay known for intricate embroidery and red-carpet eveningwear.
Dutch conceptual design duo Viktor Horsting and Rolf Snoeren, known for theatrical, art-driven couture presentations.

shows.debut: New couture house debut on the official Paris calendar
shows.venue: Garden of the Lycée Carnot, Paris
shows.bio: A newly launched couture house from Olivier Theyskens, debuting on the official Paris Haute Couture calendar.

Antwerp-trained designer Julie Kegels founded her namesake label in 2024, contrasting precision with fluidity and tradition with innovation. Her collections explore feminine archetypes through refined, sculptural construction.

Fidan Novruzova created her namesake label in October 2020 after returning to Moldova, drawing on her Azerbaijani roots. The label is known for retrofuturistic silhouettes that blend traditional craft with forward-looking design.

KIMHËKIM is the label of creative director Kiminte Kimhekim, known for a couture-influenced identity of pearls, bows and conceptual construction. The brand reworks heritage dress codes into sculptural, highly finished pieces.

Founded in Paris in September 2020 by Victor Weinsanto, Weinsanto is a theatrical luxury label spanning ready-to-wear and couture. The house mixes humor, eccentricity and precise craftsmanship into exuberant, hyper-feminine collections.

Vautrait was founded in 2021 by Yonathan Carmel as a tailoring-led house built on craftsmanship, memory and permanence. The label favors restrained, minimal design with an emphasis on cut and longevity.

Launched in South Africa in 2012 by Laduma Ngxokolo, MaXhosa Africa is a luxury knitwear label translating Xhosa beadwork into bold contemporary patterns. Its intricate knit designs have become a signature of modern African luxury.

Founded in Stockholm in 2021 by Ellen Hodakova Larsson, Hodakova transforms vintage, deadstock and discarded objects into couture-like pieces. The label is known for deconstruction and playful, one-of-a-kind upcycled design.

Founded in Montreal in 2014 by Hannah Rose Dalton and Steven Raj Bhaskaran, Matières Fécales builds a post-human glamour aesthetic of sharp tailoring and couture-like silhouettes. The duo's darkly theatrical work blurs fashion, performance and art.

Founded in 2019 by Ester Manas and Balthazar Delepierre, Ester Manas makes size-inclusive, sustainable womenswear designed to fit every body. The duo serve as the brand's artistic directors, working with deadstock and body-conscious silhouettes.
Launched in Paris in 2016 by Alexandra Golovanoff, the label centers on cashmere and knitwear. It is known for color-driven, comfortable pieces designed for longevity.
Copenhagen label that began as a cashmere knitwear line around 2000 before growing into one of Scandinavia's best-known ready-to-wear names. Ditte Reffstrup has been creative director since 2009.

Marie Adam-Leenaerdt launched her Brussels-based label in 2023 with precise, sculptural reinterpretations of everyday objects. Her multifunctional designs blend tailoring rigor with quiet conceptual play.

Founded in Tokyo in 2010 by Maiko Kurogouchi, Mame Kurogouchi blends Japanese craft with personal memory and advanced textile technology. The label is known for poetic, meticulously engineered fabrics and elegant, wearable construction.

Founded in 1946 by Christian Dior; the 1947 “New Look” reshaped postwar fashion and still anchors the house's silhouette today. Jonathan Anderson became sole creative director in 2025, the first person to oversee womenswear, menswear, and couture together.

Burç Akyol is a Paris label by French-Turkish designer Burç Akyol, known for sensual, fluid, genderless tailoring with Turkish references. His work fuses couture precision with a fluid, body-conscious sensuality.

Founded in Paris in 1988 by Martin Margiela and Jenny Meirens, Maison Margiela is defined by deconstruction, unconventional materials and its Artisanal line. Glenn Martens is the house's creative director as of 2026.

Founded in Tokyo in 2003 by Kunihiko Morinaga, Anrealage explores technology and detailed patchwork to create forms unconstrained by the conventional body. The label is known for intellectually playful, shape-shifting design.
Founded in 1961 by Yves Saint Laurent and Pierre Bergé; credited with bringing the tuxedo (Le Smoking) into womenswear. Anthony Vaccarello has been creative director since 2016.

Vaillant is the label of Alice Vaillant, known for Calais lace, jersey and asymmetry inspired by dance and the female body. Her collections celebrate movement through draped, body-conscious construction.

Founded in Paris in 2019 by artistic director Chloé Harrouche and CEO Ugo Bensoussan, Loulou de Saison offers timeless contemporary womenswear. The label is known for understated classics made from quality materials.

shows.debut: Drew Henry's first collection as creative director
shows.bio: Founded in 1961 by André Courrèges, a pioneer of 1960s space-age fashion. Drew Henry, previously senior design director at Burberry, presents his debut collection this season.

Founded in New York City in 2006 by Mary-Kate and Ashley Olsen, The Row is the standard-bearer of understated luxury. It is known for precise tailoring, premium materials and a quiet, exacting aesthetic.

Founded in 1945 by Pierre Balmain, known for sculpted, glamorous tailoring. Antonin Tron, founder of the label Atlein, became creative director in November 2025 after Olivier Rousteing’s 14-year tenure.

Founded in March 2021 by Ruohan Nie, Ruohan practices elevated minimalism through precise tailoring, exceptional fabrics and a neutral palette. The label's pared-back pieces emphasize cut and material over ornament.
Founded in 1986 by Belgian designer Dries Van Noten, one of the original “Antwerp Six.” Julian Klausner became creative director in December 2024 after Van Noten’s own retirement.

Founded in Paris in 2019 by Alphonse Maitrepierre, Maitrepierre mixes old-world fashion aesthetics with geek culture and eco-innovative materials. The house is known for theatrical, sustainability-minded collections.

Founded in 2001 by Stella McCartney in London; the house has been leather- and fur-free from day one and has since developed plant-based faux fur and lab-grown vegan silk. McCartney remains creative director of her own label.

Founded in New York in 2013 by Patric DiCaprio and now led with co-creative director Bryn Taubensee, Vaquera is known for 'fashion fan fiction' — oversized proportions and subversive, DIY-informed design. The label blends Americana references with a downtown sensibility.

Founded in 1996 in Stockholm by Jonny Johansson, part of a wider ACNE (“Ambition to Create Novel Expression”) creative collective spanning photography, art, and design. Johansson remains creative director.
Founded in 2005 by American designer Tom Ford after his tenures at Gucci and Saint Laurent. Haider Ackermann is creative director, succeeding Peter Hawkings.

Founded in 1952 by Gaby Aghion in Paris, known for its bohemian, romantic femininity. Chemena Kamali became creative director in October 2023 — her third stint at the house — succeeding Gabriela Hearst.

Junko Shimada established her design studio in Paris in 1981 after working at Cacharel, becoming one of the first Japanese designers on the French scene. Her label is known for playful ready-to-wear fusing Japanese inventiveness with French elegance.

Founded in Paris in 2023 by Alain Paul and his husband Luis Philippe, ALAINPAUL is a dance-led unisex label born from Paul's ballet training and stints at Vetements and Louis Vuitton. The house is known for sculptural silhouettes, precise tailoring and collections conceived as a choreography of fabric and body.

shows.debut: Kai Nesselrath's debut as creative director
shows.bio: Founded in 1945 by Marie-Madeleine Carven. Kai Nesselrath, who spent a decade at Saint Laurent as head designer, debuts as creative director this season, succeeding design director Mark Howard Thomas.

Founded in 1919 by Cristóbal Balenciaga in San Sebastián before relocating to Paris; long regarded as a technician's house for its sculptural tailoring. Pierpaolo Piccioli became creative director in 2025, arriving from Valentino.
Founded in 2015 by Cecilie Bahnsen in Copenhagen, known for voluminous, sculptural dresses in technical fabrics. Bahnsen remains creative director of her own label.

Uma Wang founded her namesake label with a focus on textile expertise, refined tailoring and East-West references. Known for rich material research and draped, intellectual construction, the brand bridges Chinese heritage and European craftsmanship.

Founded in Shanghai in 1997 by Shouzeng Ye and Shawna Tao, Icicle is a minimalist eco-luxury label built on natural materials and environmental responsibility. Its pared-back, nature-inspired collections are designed between Shanghai and its Paris design center.

Founded in Los Angeles in 1994 by Rick Owens, the label is known for gothic, grunge-inflected architectural silhouettes. Owens' dark, monumental aesthetic has made him one of fashion's most distinctive independent voices.

Founded in Paris in 2013 by Marie-Christine Statz, GAUCHERE is known for clean-cut tailoring and modern femininity. The label pairs minimalist formal and casual combinations with a sharp, architectural hand.
Founded by Elsa Schiaparelli in 1927, revived in 2012 and now led by Daniel Roseberry, known for surrealist, body-as-object couture. Traditionally opens the official Haute Couture calendar.
Founded in Paris in 1995 by Isabel Marant, the label defines relaxed, irreverent Parisian luxury. Marant's effortless bohemian-inflected collections blend cool nonchalance with precise craftsmanship.

Founded in 1958 when Jacques Leonard asked Daniel Tribouillard to establish Leonard Fashion, Léonard Paris is famed for vibrant floral prints, silk jersey and its orchid emblem. The house is a byword for joyous, colorful Parisian couture.
Founded in 1993 by Jun Takahashi in Tokyo, rooted in the city's punk and subculture scene. Takahashi remains creative director of his own label.

Spanish leather goods house dating to 1846 in Madrid, among the oldest names on any fashion week calendar. Jack McCollough and Lazaro Hernandez, the founders of Proenza Schouler, became co-creative directors in 2025.

The Miyake Design Studio was founded in Tokyo in 1970 by Issey Miyake, built on textile experimentation, pleating and technology. Satoshi Kondo has directed the ISSEY MIYAKE collection since Spring/Summer 2020.

Founded in 1983 by Jean-Claude Jitrois, Jitrois is a leather couture house famed for stretch leather and second-skin construction. The label's sensual, body-hugging designs are a signature of French leather luxury.

Founded in 2018 by Charaf Tajer, Casablanca is an après-sport luxury label known for hand-painted prints and relaxed, Riviera-inflected tailoring. Tajer remains the brand's founder and creative director.
Founded in 1889 by Jeanne Lanvin, the oldest French fashion house still in operation. Peter Copping is artistic director.

Founded in 2018 by Caroline Hú, Reverie by Caroline Hú is known for radical romanticism, textile craft and emotional storytelling. The label's dreamlike collections merge artisanal technique with narrative depth.

Berlin-founded, Paris-showing label by Christa Bosch and Cosima Gadient, known for raw-edged tailoring and working pre-loved pieces into its runway shows. Bosch and Gadient remain co-creative directors of their own label.

Founded in 1952 by Hubert de Givenchy, closely associated with Audrey Hepburn's screen wardrobe in the 1950s and '60s. Sarah Burton has been creative director since 2024, following two decades at Alexander McQueen.

Founded by Yohji Yamamoto, who arrived in Paris from Tokyo in 1981 alongside Rei Kawakubo and upended Western ideas of tailoring with dark, fluid, deconstructed silhouettes. Still independently owned and designed by Yamamoto himself, a rarity in the industry.
Victoria Beckham launched her namesake label in 2008, developing it in London with precise cuts and body-conscious tailoring. The brand is known for understated luxury and sharply modern femininity.
Founded in Paris in 1987 by Barbara Bui, the label is known for leather, rock energy and sharp, androgynous tailoring. Bui's collections fuse Parisian polish with a rebellious, rock-inflected edge.

Founded in 1992 by Junya Watanabe (b. 1961, Fukushima), a Rei Kawakubo protégé who trained as a Comme des Garçons patternmaker. Known as a pioneer of “techno-couture,” mixing advanced fabrics with inventive draping and construction.
Founded in 1945 by Céline Vipiana as a made-to-measure children’s shoe shop in Paris. Michael Rider became creative director in 2025, succeeding Hedi Slimane.

Launched in 2012 by Kei Ninomiya under the Comme des Garçons umbrella, Noir Kei Ninomiya is known for intricate black construction. The label's laser-cut linked pieces and minimal sewing create sculptural, technically dazzling garments.

Nehera revives the heritage of Ján Nehera's famous 1930s Czechoslovak label as an independent Slovak brand. Today's collections favor functional comfort, quiet tailoring, natural materials and sculptural volume.

Vivienne Westwood's roots lie in the London boutique she opened in 1971 with Malcolm McLaren, the cradle of punk fashion. The house remains synonymous with rebellion, historicism and unconventional tailoring; Andreas Kronthaler leads its creative direction.

French leather goods house founded in 1837 by Thierry Hermès. Nadège Vanhee-Cybulski has been artistic director of women’s ready-to-wear since 2014, prized for a decade-long tenure of stability in an industry defined by rotation.

Launched in Paris in March 2021 by Vincent Garnier Pressiat, Pressiat is a no-gender label of provocative Parisian elegance. The collections fuse architecture, craft and nightlife into sensual, boundary-pushing design.
Founded by Lebanese designer Elie Saab in 1982, a couture mainstay known for intricate embroidery and red-carpet eveningwear.
Founded in 1969 by Rei Kawakubo in Tokyo, long associated with deconstruction and challenging conventional ideas of beauty. Kawakubo remains creative director of her own label.

Founded by Azzedine Alaïa, the house is celebrated for sculptural, body-conscious silhouettes and precision cutting. Pieter Mulier has been creative director since 2021, continuing Alaïa's legacy of exacting craftsmanship.
Founded by Belgian designer Ann Demeulemeester, another of the “Antwerp Six,” known for dark, poetic tailoring. Stefano Gallici has been creative director since June 2023.

Founded in South-East London in 1970 by Margaret Howell, the label is known for understated, functional British clothing. Natural textures and timeless construction define its quietly confident aesthetic.
Founded in 1933 by tennis champion René Lacoste and André Gillier, Lacoste is famed for the L.12.12 polo and its crocodile emblem. The house blends sportswear heritage with contemporary French style.

The Paris couture house Dice Kayek was founded in 1992 by Turkish sisters Ece and Ayşe Ege. Known for sculptural, architectural 'modern romantic' design in luxurious fabrics, the house is led creatively by Ece.

Founded in Barcelona in 2014 by Paloma Lanna and Tana Latorre, Paloma Wool is an art-meets-fashion project known for expressive knitwear. Local production, collaborations and small runs define its intimate, creative spirit.

Niccolò Pasqualetti founded his eponymous label in 2021, working between Paris and Tuscany with local artisans. The label is known for sculptural, gender-inclusive clothing with deconstructed volumes and subtle palettes.
Launched in 1993 by Miuccia Prada as a younger, more experimental sister label to Prada. Miuccia Prada remains its creative director.

Founded in St. Gallen in 1922 by Alice Kriemler-Schoch, Akris is known for textile innovation, double-face construction and understated luxury. Albert Kriemler serves as the house's creative director.

Mossi Traoré launched his Paris-area womenswear label in 2017 with a vision of urban contemporary couture. Pleating, drape and architectural silhouettes — often developed through artistic collaborations — define the house.
Founded in 1960 by Valentino Garavani, who died in January 2026. Alessandro Michele became creative director in March 2024, succeeding Pierpaolo Piccioli after his 25-year tenure.

Founded by Thierry Mugler, the house is known for theatrical, architectural, body-conscious fashion. Casey Cadwallader is reported as its current creative director, carrying forward Mugler's powerful, sculpted aesthetic.

Founded by Jean Paul Gaultier in 1976. After years of rotating guest designers presenting couture under his name, Duran Lantink was named permanent creative director in 2026 to carry the house's sculptural, boundary-pushing legacy forward.
Founded in 1999 by Chitose Abe in Tokyo, known for “splicing” two or more garments into one hybrid piece. Abe remains creative director of her own label.

Founded in 1952 in Monestier-de-Clermont by René Ramillon and André Vincent, Moncler is the benchmark for technical luxury down outerwear. The brand fuses mountain heritage with high-fashion collaborations.
Founded in Paris in 1965 by Emanuel Ungaro, the house is known for bold color, mixed prints and sensual draping. Ungaro's creations balance seductive femininity with couture-level craftsmanship.
Founded in Taipei in 1978 by Wang Chen Tsai-Hsia and Wang Yuan-Hong, Shiatzy Chen pioneered 'neo-Chinese chic.' The house fuses Chinese aesthetic heritage with refined contemporary design.

Founded in Paris in 2019 by Spanish designer Abraham Ortuño Perez, Abra is an accessories-led label known for shoes, bags and surreal, spiky details. Spanish craftsmanship underpins its playful, offbeat luxury.

Founded in New York in 2015 by Gabriela Hearst, the label stands for 'honest luxury' — sustainability, artisanal craftsmanship and modern classics. Hearst's restrained, material-driven design has made her a leading voice in responsible fashion.
Showing on the Paris Spring/Summer 2027 calendar; profile to be confirmed.

Founded in Sydney in 1991 by sisters Nicky and Simone Zimmermann, the label is known for sophisticated femininity, color and original prints across swim and ready-to-wear. Nicky Zimmermann serves as creative director.

Kiko Kostadinov is a London label founded by Bulgarian designer Kiko Kostadinov, known for workwear, uniforms and functional details. His experimental construction reworks utilitarian references into refined, forward-thinking design.

Austrian designer Florentina Leitner launched her namesake London label at the end of 2020. The brand is known for playful prints, colorful textiles and elegant cuts that blend wit with precise construction.
Founded in Paris in 1975 by Agnès Troublé, agnès b. is known for simple, timeless clothing — including the iconic snap cardigan. The brand's understated French style has endured as a wardrobe staple.

French couture house founded in 1910 by Gabrielle “Coco” Chanel; built its identity on tweed suiting, the little black dress, and No. 5. Matthieu Blazy has been creative director since 2025, arriving from Bottega Veneta.

The Parisian house XULY.Bët was founded in 1992 by Malian designer Lamine Kouyaté. A pioneer of upcycling and reconstructed clothing, the label fuses African references with subversive, eco-responsible fashion.

Ujoh is a Japanese label founded in 2009 by Mitsuru Nishizaki, led by a pattern-cutter's sensibility. Precise tailoring, asymmetrical cuts and inventive construction define its quietly technical collections.

Founded in Kyiv in 2009 by Lilia Litkovska, Litkovska is known for architectural tailoring, deconstruction and transformable garments. The label's conceptual, sculptural pieces reflect its Ukrainian roots and avant-garde spirit.

Founded in Sydney in 2010 by Christopher Esber, the label is known for sensual deconstruction — sculptural silhouettes, cut-outs and precise fabric techniques. Esber's work balances minimalism with body-conscious allure.

Founded in Tokyo in 2020 by Yusuke Takahashi, CFCL creates computer-developed 3D knitwear from sustainable materials. The label's seamless, tech-driven knits offer a modern uniform of effortless precision.

Founded in Seoul in 2013 by Hyemee Lee, EENK is known for its Letter Project — collectible, structural pieces with a vintage-classic sensibility. The label reworks wardrobe staples through a distinctly Korean design lens.

Founded in 2019 by Di Du between Shanghai and Paris, Didu explores subversive, body-conscious femininity in sustainable fabrics. The label's provocative, precisely cut pieces channel a bold, contemporary sensuality.

Founded in Tbilisi in 2015 by Irakli Rusadze and Davit Giorgadze, Situationist channels Georgian heritage through structured leather and oversized tailoring. The label is known for sculptural, gender-fluid design with a post-Soviet edge.

Founded in Paris in 2017 by Maria Boyarovskaya and Artem Kononenko, Boyarovskaya practices 'emotional minimalism.' Clean lines, elaborate knits and deconstructed tailoring define the house, with Maria Boyarovskaya as artistic director.

Pierre Cardin founded his couture house in Paris in 1950, pioneering geometric, futuristic Space Age fashion. Rodrigo Basilicati-Cardin became artistic director in December 2020, continuing the house's avant-garde legacy.
Founded in 1854 by Louis Vuitton as a Parisian trunk maker, long before it became a ready-to-wear house. Nicolas Ghesquière has led womenswear since 2013; Pharrell Williams leads menswear.

Vivienne Westwood was founded in 1971 in London by Vivienne Westwood and Malcolm McLaren, emerging from their King's Road shop into a defining force in punk fashion. Its bridal line — Bridal Couture, Made to Order, and AK for VW — has been a cult favorite since Westwood's own SS1992 runway debut of bridalwear; the house staged its first-ever full bridal fashion show in 2025.
Israeli bridal house founded in 2004 by Berta Balilti, a Shenkar College graduate now based in Ashdod, Israel, known for bold, figure-hugging silhouettes and dramatic embellishment.

Founded in 1984 in Tel Aviv by Galia Lahav; in 2017 became the first Israeli brand accepted into the Chambre Syndicale de la Haute Couture and to present at Paris Fashion Week. Known for sheer overlays, corsetry, and romantic, couture-level craftsmanship.

Hayley Paige Gutman entered bridal design in 2011 at age 25, known for playful, whimsical gowns. After a multi-year legal dispute over rights to her own name, she relaunched independently under Hayley Paige in 2024; her REIN collection drew on equestrian tradition and Belle Époque ornamentation.

Israeli designer Pnina Tornai began making wedding dresses in 1992 and has partnered with New York's Kleinfeld Bridal — the salon behind TLC's Say Yes to the Dress — for two decades, known for her signature sexy, corset-driven silhouettes.

Founded in 1984 in Toronto by Ines Di Santo, an Italian-Argentine designer known for glamorous, art-influenced bridal and eveningwear couture. Her daughter Veronica joined the business in 1998 and now serves as managing partner.
Founded in 1986 in Dallas by Vatana Watters, known for sculptural silhouettes and handcrafted detail across its Watters, Wtoo, and Willowby collections.

Founded in 1985 by Amsale Aberra and Neil Brown after Aberra, an Ethiopian American designer, couldn't find a simply modern gown for her own wedding. Aberra became the first Black woman inducted into the CFDA; she died in 2018 and the house continues under her name, with a flagship in SoHo.

American leather goods house founded in 1941 in New York; Stuart Vevers has been creative director since 2013, leaning the house into youthful, downtown Americana. Its (Re)Loved program repairs, restores, and buys back used Coach pieces for resale.

shows.venue: Jack Shainman Gallery, Tribeca, downtown Manhattan, New York (third consecutive season in the space)
shows.bio: Founded in 1967 by Ralph Lauren, built on an aspirational, preppy vision of American style — the polo player logo among the most recognized in fashion.

shows.venue: Gilder Center at the American Museum of Natural History, New York
shows.bio: Founded in 2012 by Jasmin Larian in Los Angeles, best known for its bamboo Ark bag and resort-driven silhouettes.

shows.venue: Judson Memorial Church (Judson Theatre), 243 Thompson Street, Greenwich Village, New York
shows.bio: Founded in 2001 by Rachel Comey in New York, known for architectural, artisanal womenswear with an unconventional edge; celebrated its 25th anniversary this season.

shows.venue: The National Arts Club, 15 Gramercy Park South
shows.bio: Founded in 2000 by Johnson Hartig in Los Angeles, known for whimsical, screen-printed, embellished pieces built from vintage and secondhand garments.

shows.debut: Henry Zankov's runway debut as artistic director
shows.venue: Under the High Line, New York
shows.bio: Founded in 1970 by Diane von Furstenberg, best known for inventing the wrap dress in 1974. Henry Zankov became artistic director in 2026, the brand's first appointment to that role.
Founded in 2016 by Emily Adams Bode Aujla in New York, built around vintage quilts, antique textiles, and other repurposed material. Bode Aujla remains creative director of her own label.

Founded in 2011 by Mike Eckhaus and Zoe Latta in Los Angeles, now showing in New York; known for raw, unfinished-looking construction and a longstanding pre-loved runway partnership with eBay. Eckhaus and Latta remain co-creative directors of their own label.

shows.venue: The Grill's Pool Room, Midtown, New York
shows.bio: American designer based between London and New York, known for upcycling deadstock fabric and secondhand garments into new pieces. Ives remains creative director of his own label.
Founded in 2016 by Catherine Holstein in New York, known for elevated, quietly sexy basics. Holstein remains creative director of her own label.

shows.venue: Former Rubin Museum, West 17th Street, New York (building formerly housed the Barneys New York women's store; models descended the central spiral staircase)
shows.bio: Founded in 2002 by Jack McCollough and Lazaro Hernandez, then Parsons classmates, in New York. Rachel Scott became creative director in 2026 after the founders' move to Loewe.

shows.venue: Sotheby's (Marcel Breuer building), Madison Avenue, New York
shows.bio: Founded in 2004 by Tory Burch in New York, built around a preppy-with-an-edge American style. Burch remains creative director of her own label.

shows.venue: The Shed, Hudson Yards, New York City
shows.bio: Founded in 2001 by Thom Browne in New York, built around a signature shrunken gray suit and reinventions of American tailoring. Browne remains creative director of his own label.
Founded in 1999 by Sabyasachi Mukherjee in Kolkata, known for opulent, heavily embroidered Indian bridal and couture work. Mukherjee remains creative director of his own label.

shows.venue: TWP's SoHo building, 21 Howard Street, New York City
shows.bio: New York-based womenswear label founded by Trish Wescoat Pound, dedicated to reimagining the modern woman's closet.

shows.venue: Balloon Museum at South Street Seaport, New York
shows.bio: Founded in 2021 by Terrence Zhou, a New York-based designer known for maximalist, fantastical silhouettes — balloon gowns, sculptural creature-inspired pieces — worn by Rina Sawayama and Christina Aguilera.
Founded in 1985 by Tommy Hilfiger, built around preppy American sportswear and the brand's signature flag logo.
Founded in 2002 by Stacey Bendet in New York, known for flirty, print-driven contemporary womenswear.
Founded in 2012 by South African-born designer Daniella Kallmeyer in New York, known for fluid, body-conscious tailoring.

shows.venue: the new Dante on Elizabeth Street in Nolita
shows.bio: Founded in 2013 by Rebecca Hessel Cohen in New York, known for romantic, ruffled florals and immersive, theatrical presentations.
Founded in 2008 by Christian Siriano, who won the fourth season of Project Runway that same year; known for red-carpet gowns in extended size ranges.
Founded in 2008 by Dao-Yi Chow and Maxwell Osborne in New York, known for elevating utilitarian streetwear into tailored ready-to-wear.

New York-based designer known for technology-enhanced shape engineering and fabric-first, sculptural experimentation over traditional themed collections. Named to the Forbes 30 Under 30 list in 2025; worn by Beyoncé and Katy Perry.
Founded in 1981 by Michael Kors in New York, built around jet-set American luxury sportswear.
Houston-born designer Amir Taghi (b. 1996) began designing as a teenager, interning with Oscar de la Renta before making his NYFW debut in 2014.
Founded in 1996 in New York, known for wearable, tailored contemporary womenswear rather than runway spectacle.
Founded by Jackson Wiederhoeft in New York, known for corsetry-driven, exaggerated eveningwear silhouettes.
One of New York's newer womenswear designers, known for a considered, unconventional approach to dressing.
Founded by Christian Cowan, known for maximalist, sequined eveningwear with a camp sensibility.

shows.venue: Skylight at the Refinery, Brooklyn (glass dome atop the former Domino Sugar factory)
shows.bio: Founded in 2015 by Laura Kim and Fernando Garcia, who are also co-creative directors of Oscar de la Renta.
Founded by Kim Shui, a Hong Kong-born, New York-based designer known for glossy, futuristic party clothes.

shows.venue: Phillips auction house on Park Avenue
shows.bio: Founded in 2004 by Jonathan Simkhai in Los Angeles, known for body-conscious eveningwear and knitwear.

shows.venue: Greenhouse in Greenpoint, Brooklyn, New York
shows.bio: Rio Uribe founded Gypsy Sport in 2012 after working his way up to head of merchandising at Balenciaga, building a brand known for gender-fluid, inclusive casting and streetwear-luxury mixes.

Eritrean-born designer Nardos Imam launched her namesake luxury house in 2012 after training in costume design and working as in-house designer at Dallas' Stanley Korshak. Flagships in Dallas and on Madison Avenue, NYC.

shows.venue: Woolworth Building (Gilded Age lobby), Lower Manhattan
shows.bio: Founded in 2008 by Joseph Altuzarra in New York, known for sensual, body-conscious tailoring.

shows.venue: 100 Feast (Cantonese banquet hall), Chinatown, New York
shows.bio: Los Angeles-based label launched in 2022 by Kari Vettese, drawing on her Italian heritage; worn by Charli XCX, Florence Pugh, and Kylie Jenner.

shows.debut: Nicola Brognano's runway debut as creative director
shows.bio: Founded in 2000, one of the brands credited with launching the premium denim category. Nicola Brognano, formerly of Blumarine, became creative director in 2026.

shows.venue: The National Arts Club, Gramercy Park, New York
shows.bio: Founded in 1981 by Anna Sui in New York, known for bohemian, vintage-referencing prints.
Founded in 1997 by Amy Smilovic, known for elevated, texture-driven contemporary basics.

Founded in 2020 by Seoul-born designer Ashlynn Park in New York, Ashlyn is known for precision tailoring, sculptural draping, and a zero-waste approach to luxury womenswear. Park, who studied architecture before fashion, won the 2025 CFDA/Vogue Fashion Fund and the 2025 CFDA American Emerging Designer of the Year award.
Founded in 2009 by Prabal Gurung in New York, known for bold color and a strong focus on inclusivity in casting.
Founded in 2014 by Colm Dillane in New York, blending streetwear with theatrical, narrative-driven runway presentations.
Founded in 1998 in New York (originally as As Four), a design collective known for geometric, sculptural, and technology-driven garments.
shows.cd: Gabi Asfour, Adi Gil, Angela Donhauser (founding trio)

shows.bio: Milwaukee-born, Puerto Rican-heritage designer Elena Velez (b. 1994) trained at Parsons and Central Saint Martins, known for synthesizing metalsmithing with high fashion. Named CFDA's 2022 Emerging Designer of the Year.
Denim-focused ready-to-wear label founded by Fforme co-founder Nina Khosla and Talia Shuvalov (ex-Alexander McQueen, Alexander Wang), with Joey Laurenti (ex-Sies Marjan, Opening Ceremony) as CEO.
Founded in 2013 by Piotrek Panszczyk and Beckett Fogg in New York, known for maximalist crystal embellishment.
New York-based designer known for romantic, body-focused ready-to-wear built from deadstock materials into sculptural, historically-informed silhouettes.

shows.venue: WSA building, 161 Water Street, Financial District, New York
shows.bio: Launched in 2007 as a more considered, design-led sister brand to H&M.

shows.venue: Petzel Gallery, Chelsea, New York City
shows.bio: Founded in 2014 by Sandy Liang in New York, known for girlish, nostalgic downtown style.
Founded in 2013 by Polish designer Magda Butrym, known for florals and body-conscious silhouettes.

Founded in 2017 by Patricio Campillo, a Mexico City-born designer known for rigorous tailoring referencing charro culture and ranch life, sourced from small artisan workshops in Mexico. LVMH Prize semi-finalist, 2024.

shows.venue: Rainbow Room, 30 Rockefeller Plaza (Rockefeller Center), New York City
shows.bio: Founded in 2016 by Sergio Hudson in South Carolina, known for power tailoring popularized by Kamala Harris and Beyoncé.
Founded in 2015 by Brandon Maxwell, who first came up styling and designing for Lady Gaga.
Founded in 2011 by Todd Snyder, known for reworking classic American menswear.
New York-based designer known for liquid-metal, biomechanical sculptural pieces that blur fashion and body armor.

shows.venue: Hotel Chelsea (El Quijote restaurant / Bard Room)
shows.bio: Founded by costume and fashion designer Zaldy Goco, known for his long-running collaboration with Lady Gaga.

Trinidad-born designer Aisling Camps trained as a mechanical engineer before studying at Columbia University and the Fashion Institute of Technology. Known for sculptural, architectural knitwear made from Italian-sourced yarns out of her Brooklyn studio.

shows.venue: Gotham Park, under the Brooklyn Bridge overpass, New York
shows.bio: Founded in 1998 by Ulla Johnson in New York, known for artisanal detailing and a bohemian sensibility.
Founded in 1967 by Norma Kamali, a pioneer of the sleeping-bag coat and the modern swimsuit-as-outerwear silhouette.

Luxury womenswear label co-founded in 2022 by Nina Khosla (product designer, also of Ossou) and Laura Vazquez (former EVP of Jil Sander Navy and Perry Ellis), built on a tech-inflected, slow-fashion, direct-to-consumer model. Creative direction has changed hands since launch.
Founded by Zane Li, a 2026 CFDA/Vogue Fashion Fund finalist.
Los Angeles-based footwear and accessories designer Jamie Haller, known for sculptural heels and a Montecito retail store.
Fine jewelry label founded by George Inaki Root, working primarily in freshwater pearls.

Founded in 2024 by Julia 'Juju' Ferentinos in New York City, known for sculptural, antique-inspired jewelry drawing on Art Deco, 1990s editorials, and Greco-Roman heritage. The Petra pendant became a signature piece.

Founded in 2019 by Emily Dawn Long in New York, known for vintage-inspired, artisanal gender-fluid pieces with cheeky, irreverent humor. Her crochet 'Hat Named Wanda' is a celebrity favorite, and she was nominated for the 2026 CFDA Emerging Designer of the Year award.
New York label founded by Claire Sullivan, a Vaquera co-founder who went solo in 2022, known for playful, culturally referential eveningwear.
Founded in 2020 by Henry Zankov in New York, known for colorful, playful knitwear. Zankov also became Diane von Furstenberg's artistic director in 2026.

Founded in 2016 by China-born Parsons graduates Siying Qu and Haoran Li, a genderless New York label that treats each season like a newspaper dispatch, using collections to explore a social issue the duo is passionate about — from coral reef preservation to pharmaceutical corruption. A 2019 CFDA/Vogue Fashion Fund finalist.
Founded in 2021 by Rachel Scott, drawing on Jamaican craft techniques like crochet; Scott also became Proenza Schouler's creative director in 2026.

shows.venue: The Pierre Hotel, Upper East Side, New York
shows.bio: Founded in 2008 by Bibhu Mohapatra, known for intricately embroidered eveningwear.

shows.venue: David H. Koch Theater, New York
shows.bio: Founded in 1981 by Carolina Herrera, long associated with ladylike tailoring and dramatic white shirting.

shows.venue: the Unisphere, Flushing Meadows–Corona Park, Queens
shows.bio: Founded in 2016 by Raúl López in New York, known for reworking utilitarian and streetwear shapes into elevated pieces.
Founded in 2009 by LaQuan Smith in Queens, New York, known for body-conscious, sex-positive eveningwear.
Namesake label of Kozaburo Akasaka (b. 1984, Tokyo), who graduated from Central Saint Martins with a first-class degree in menswear.
Luxury womenswear label built around the idea of forgotten traditions, founded by Stephanie Suberville and her husband Jeffrey Axford.
Fashion and media brand founded in Sacramento in 2014 by Keith “Rooftop” Herron, who started the brand at age 14 selling handmade stickers.

shows.venue: Storm King Art Center, Hudson Valley, New York
shows.bio: Founded in 2010 by Hillary Taymour in New York, known for upcycled fabrics and maximalist prints layered with an environmental message.

shows.venue: St. Bartholomew's Church (St. Bart's), Park Avenue, New York
shows.bio: Founded in 2021 by Andrew Kwon in New York, built around eveningwear and bridal, worn by Regina Hall, Lucy Liu, and Sophia Bush on red carpets.
Founded in 2016 by Stephanie Pollack in Los Angeles, known for elevated, deconstructed denim and basics.
American designer who launched his eponymous label in the 1980s; credited with bringing grunge to the runway in 1992. Jacobs remains creative director of his own label.

Founded in 1968 by Calvin Klein, long defined by minimalist tailoring and its signature underwear and jeans lines. Veronica Leoni became creative director of Calvin Klein Collection in 2025, continuing the house's exploration of American minimalism.
Founded by Frederick Anderson, known for bold color and print in eveningwear.

Founded in 1979 by Irish designer Paul Costelloe, who was personal designer to Diana, Princess of Wales, from 1983 until her death. Costelloe passed away in November 2025; his son William Costelloe has since taken over as creative director.
Founded by Georgian designer Lado Keburia, known for architectural minimalism, monochromatic palettes, and gender-fluid silhouettes.

Founded during the pandemic by couple George Oxby and Angus Cockram in London, known for corsetry, tailoring and leatherwork with an irreverent 'harmonious chaos' edge. After years as a bespoke atelier dressing Beyoncé and Lady Gaga (plus custom looks for RAYE, Madonna, PinkPantheress, Zara Larsson and BTS), the label made its official runway debut with the SS26 'Prophet' collection.
Derbyshire-born designer who enrolled at Central Saint Martins in 2022 and has worked at both Vivienne Westwood and Mulberry, running his independent label from South London alongside his studies.
Founded by Demon Zhang, blending Eastern philosophical approaches with Western construction techniques through artistic prints and sophisticated silhouettes.
Canadian-born, London-based knitwear designer known for figure-hugging silhouettes and for pioneering size-inclusive runway casting in the late 2000s.
Founded in 2020 by Harris Reed in London, known for theatrical, gender-fluid silhouettes. Reed has also been creative director of Nina Ricci in Paris since 2022.

Now in its third year, eBay Endless Runway is the only pre-loved, shoppable show on the official London Fashion Week schedule, staged in partnership with the British Fashion Council. Every look is made entirely from pre-loved fashion and can be bought in real time via eBay Live during the show.

Founded in 1947 by Erling Persson in Västerås, Sweden, known for affordable fast fashion and high-profile designer collaborations. One of the world's largest clothing retailers, it staged an immersive see-now-buy-now event on the LFW SS27 calendar on September 17, 2026.

Founded in 2011 by married couple Ksenia and Anton Schnaider in Kyiv, known for reworked, upcycled, and patchwork denim — including their signature “demi-denim” culotte-jean hybrid, originally made from secondhand denim.
Swedish designer and recent Central Saint Martins MA graduate, a 2026 LVMH Prize finalist making her LFW runway debut as a BFC NEWGEN recipient this season.

shows.venue: St Cyprian's Church, Clarence Gate, Marylebone (near Regent's Park)
shows.bio: Turkish-born, London-based designer who founded his label in 2002 after graduating from Central Saint Martins’ MA program, where Domenico Dolce and Stefano Gabbana purchased pieces from his graduate collection. Known for romantic, “dark romanticism” silhouettes.
Central Saint Martins graduate Susan Fang is known for hand-crafted glass-bead accessories and her signature “air-weaving” technique, lacing layered materials into 3-dimensional forms.

shows.venue: ICA (Institute of Contemporary Arts), The Mall, London
shows.bio: British designer born in Dubai (1988), graduated from the University of Westminster in 2012, and showed with the Fashion East incubator for three seasons before her solo LFW runway debut in September 2014. A repeat BFC NEWGEN recipient.

Beijing-raised, Central Saint Martins-trained (BA and MA) designer who co-founded his eponymous brand with Yibo Chen (Royal College of Art). Focused on gender-neutral fashion, innovative knitwear, and sustainable textile practices.

Founded in 2025 by Matt Empringham and Freddy Coomes in London, known for experimental textile work — including garments made from paper — and a slightly off-kilter take on archetypal British staples. The duo met on the first day of their foundation course at Central Saint Martins; the label was originally called Aletta before they renamed it A Letter and staged their debut runway show under the new name at LFW SS27.

shows.venue: Palace x Nike skatespace at Manor Place
shows.bio: Not a single label but a nonprofit talent incubator founded by Lulu Kennedy in 2000, staging group runway shows for emerging London designers each season since 2003, with backing from Topshop and the Greater London Authority.

shows.venue: Courtyard of Skinners' Hall (Grade I listed), City of London
shows.bio: Founded in 2018 by Annie Doble in Ibiza, known for maximalist vintage-inspired glamour, bold embellishment and occasion dressing. Doble started out buying and selling vintage as a teenager before opening her first boutique in Ibiza's Old Town with £200; her celebrity clients have included Kate Moss, Taylor Swift and Margot Robbie.

East London designer known for tailoring-driven collections and immersive, party-style show formats staged in nightclub and subculture-adjacent venues, often working with Savile Row-trained tailor Charlie Allen.
Founded by Natasha Zinko, a London-based, Odesa-born designer trained at Central Saint Martins. Works largely from deadstock fabric in a closed-loop production cycle.

shows.venue: St Cuthbert's Church, Earls Court, London
shows.bio: Welsh designer who founded his namesake house in 2022, working entirely by hand with plant-based, recycled, organic, and repurposed materials and natural dyes (logwood, madder, turmeric, onion skins). A 2024 LVMH Prize finalist and Sarabande Foundation resident.

Founded by Talia Lipkin-Connor, a Central Saint Martins 2020 graduate, and named for her great uncle’s Liverpool boutique Lucinda Byre. East London-based, built on heritage, ritual, and longevity over output.
London-based designer from Liverpool, working with upcycled materials and circular design principles; founded London Fashion Week's first Swap Shop.
Founded in the 1980s by John Richmond after graduating Kingston University in 1982; co-founded the Richmond-Cornejo label with Maria Cornejo in 1984 before launching his own eponymous line.

Founded by Priya Ahluwalia in London, built on upcycled and recycled materials and drawing on her Nigerian, Indian, and British heritage. Ahluwalia won the Queen Elizabeth II Award for British Design in 2021.

Paris-born designer who studied at École Duperré before a Central Saint Martins MA, working for Simone Rocha, Rejina Pyo, and Alexander Wang before launching her own hand-knit-driven label in 2022. Winner of the ANDAM Special Prize 2026 and a 2024 LVMH Prize finalist.

shows.venue: Somerset House, outdoor terrace (under a tent overlooking the Thames), London
shows.bio: Founded in 1997 by Yasuko Furuta in Tokyo, known for playful layered dressing, deconstructed silhouettes and unexpected combinations of pattern and texture. The main line has been presented in London since AW14; the brand approaches its 30th anniversary in 2027, with the TOGA PULLA diffusion line and TOGA VIRILIS menswear line under the same house.

shows.venue: St Bartholomew's Hospital, North Wing, London
shows.bio: Norwegian-born, London-based designer Eli Khzouz presents sustainable luxury built on organic materials and a zero-waste approach.

shows.venue: Pentagon Hall at Ark Globe Academy, South London
shows.bio: Founded in 2017 by Charlotte Knowles and Alexandre Arsenault in London, known for lingerie-inflected, technical, body-conscious womenswear.
Founded by Richard Quinn in London, known for lavish, floral-printed eveningwear and a monarchy-adjacent following (the Queen once attended his show).
London-based designer trained at Central Saint Martins, whose work explores traditional Asian ideals of feminine beauty through delicate, romantic silhouettes.

Founded by Emma Chopova and Laura Lowena in London, known for kilts and pieces built from recycled materials and deadstock textiles like pillowcases and aprons. Chopova and Lowena remain co-creative directors of their own label.
Founded in 2010 by Simone Rocha in London, known for pairing romantic, feminine fabrics with harder, more confrontational details. Rocha remains creative director of her own label.

shows.venue: Haverstock School gymnasium, Chalk Farm, north London
shows.bio: Vancouver-born, Korean-Canadian designer trained at Central Saint Martins, with early experience under Alexander McQueen, John Galliano, and Zac Posen before launching her own London label.
Founded in 2005 by Erdem Moralioğlu in London, known for painterly florals and literary, historical references. Moralioğlu remains creative director of his own label.
Founded in 2014 by Foday Dumbuya, blending British tailoring with West African heritage and craftsmanship.
British leather goods house founded in 1971; Christopher Kane took over as creative director in 2026.

British-Cypriot designer Charlie Constantinou founded his label in 2022 after a Central Saint Martins MA, building modular, adaptable garments from deadstock fabrics and artisanal hand-dyeing. An LVMH Prize semi-finalist (2023) who has collaborated with 66°North and Demon Footwear.

shows.venue: Natural Dye and Wellbeing Garden, National Theatre, London
shows.bio: Founded by Roksanda Ilincic in London, known for architectural color-blocked silhouettes.

Founded in 2014 by Kanyinsola Onalaja in London, Onalaja is known for maximalist demi-couture that combines African craft traditions with hand embroidery, beadwork and sculptural embellishment. The label offers an unusually broad size range, from XXS to XXXXL, and has been worn by Tems, Olivia Dean and Ciara.
Founded by Lee Alexander McQueen in 1992, known for its theatrical, precisely tailored, and often confrontational take on British fashion. Seán McGirr has been creative director since 2023.

London-based label founded in 2020 by multidisciplinary artist Ronan Mckenzie. The name draws from the Ghanaian Ewe word for ‘God hears me,’ with collections exploring tactility and structure alongside Mckenzie’s wider practice in scent, furniture, and performance.

Founded in 2014 by Amrita Khanna and Gursi Singh in New Delhi, known for anti-fit graphic pieces blending a minimalist, modern aesthetic with handcrafted Indian textiles. Run independently and collaboratively by the husband-and-wife duo, the label grew from a Delhi vintage shop into one of India's most talked-about contemporary brands; SS27 'India: IYKYK' was their London Fashion Week debut.
Founded by Greek designer Dimitra Petsa, known for her signature “wet look” draping technique that gives garments the appearance of being freshly emerged from water.

Launched in 2022 by Liza Keane in London, known for subversive womenswear and menswear that treats fabric and leather as sculptural media — garments as sensual second skins and psychological armour, informed by philosophers such as Georges Bataille and Carl Jung. A BFC NewGen recipient, she staged her debut LFW runway show for SS27 with 'Rain On My Parade'.

Founded in 1856 by Thomas Burberry in Basingstoke, England; invented gabardine and popularized the trench coat. Daniel Lee has been creative director since 2022. ReBurberry Services offers repair, reproofing, and restoration for existing pieces.
Founded in 2006 by Stine Goya in Copenhagen, known for bold color and print in otherwise minimal Scandinavian silhouettes.
Founded in 2001 by Henrik Vibskov in Copenhagen, known for theatrical runway sets and sculptural, textile-driven menswear and womenswear.
Founded in 2003 by Malene Birger in Copenhagen, known for fluid, elevated ready-to-wear in muted tones.
Danish label founded by Naja Munthe, known for bohemian-tinged, texture-driven ready-to-wear.
Copenhagen label known for quiet, minimalist basics made with an emphasis on organic and traceable materials.

Founded in 2019 by Awa Malina Stelter and Stephanie Gundelach in Copenhagen, known for wearable, accessible wardrobe staples blending Parisian chic ("Opéra") with a sporty Danish edge ("Sport"), produced from recycled or organic fabrics. Notable: opened its first physical store in Copenhagen in 2025; admirers include Kourtney Kardashian and Danish style icon Pernille Teisbaek.

shows.debut: CPHFW International Guest Slot, supported by The Climate Pledge
shows.venue: Waterfront, in front of the Copenhagen Opera House
shows.bio: Founded in 2010 by Hillary Taymour in New York, known for upcycled fabrics and maximalist prints layered with an environmental message.

Founded in 1983 by Franco Moschino in Milan, built on a tradition of pointed, satirical takes on fashion itself. Loris Messina and Simone Rizzo, formerly of Sunnei, were named co-creative directors in 2026.
Founded in 1988 by Woo Youngmi in Seoul; one of the first Korean designers to build a presence on the Paris runway calendar. Woo remains creative director of her own label.

shows.venue: Lotte World Mall World Park, Seoul (outdoor lawn against Lotte World Tower)
shows.bio: Paris-based label known for playful, sculptural takes on everyday dressing.
Chinese designer and Central Saint Martins graduate known for bold prints that mix traditional Chinese motifs with streetwear shapes. Chen remains creative director of her own label.

Founded in 2017 by Marine Serre in Paris; builds every collection from upcycled deadstock and surplus fabric rather than new material. Serre remains creative director of her own label. In July 2026 the label's parent company entered redressement judiciaire (French court-supervised restructuring) amid cash-flow pressure; the company remains operational and is seeking an investor.
Brazilian designer showing in São Paulo, working across resort and eveningwear.
Founded in 2011 by Adebayo Oke-Lawal in Lagos, known for gender-fluid menswear rooted in Nigerian identity and storytelling. Oke-Lawal remains creative director of his own label.
Made-in-Los-Angeles vegan label founded by Rooney Mara, built entirely from animal-free materials. Mara remains creative director of her own label.

Copenhagen label founded by designer couple Jens Skov Østergaard and Kridpat Charoenchaipiyakul, uniting their respective cultures; the SS27 collection 'Sea Marked', shown as a CPHFW One To Watch, drew on the Skagen Painters and Asian seafaring traditions.

Launched in September 2021 by weaver and textile designer Sarah Brunnhuber, Stem is a zero-waste woven-garment label whose loom-to-garment system eliminates production waste; its SS27 collection included one-off upcycled looks made from Ganni deadstock.

Launched in 2024 by Danish designer Peter Jensen, Yours Truly is a sustainable brand made and produced in Denmark, Los Angeles and Atlanta, run as a platform for artist collaborations; known for playful, muse-driven presentations casting women over 50.

Copenhagen-based ready-to-wear and demi-couture studio founded in 2024 by Freyja Taus and Juho Lehiö, blending elevated essentials with subversion, grounded in upcycling, intentional construction and archival research.

Eponymous label by Danish designer Anne Sofie Madsen, combining traditional craftsmanship with alternative materials and experimental technologies; the SS27 collection 'The New Desire' was accompanied by a live flute performance by Danish artist Michala Petri.
Copenhagen label designed by Freya Dalsjø, Karis Dalsjø and Mikkel Schou, focused on intricate craft and natural materials.
Humanwear label founded by Alectra Rothschild, spanning craft, performance, identity and counterculture.

Graduate showcase from the Royal Danish Academy's Fashion, Clothing and Textiles programme ('New Landscapes for Change'), Scandinavia's leading design academy, rooted in sustainability and material resourcefulness.

SAFD's SS27 graduate showcase presented 27 individual collections, blending traditional craft with laser cutting, digital knitting and 3D-printed details; Denmark's oldest fashion and design school, based in central Copenhagen.

shows.venue: Sankt Annæ Plads, Copenhagen (outdoor street show)
shows.bio: Copenhagen tailoring house founded in 2014 under creative director Caroline Engelgaar, known for refined modern tailoring and natural materials; SS27 'The Dark Light of Summer' was staged as an outdoor street show.

Swedish brand founded in 2019 by Rebecca Dovenryd Almberg, championing 'feral luxury' — quality garments designed to be reused, recycled and resold; the first Swedish brand admitted to the CPHFW NEWTALENT programme, with SS27 its debut show.
Danish womenswear brand founded in 2008 by Sanne Sehested, known for a vintage- and rock-inspired twist on Scandi style.

Swedish label by Yulia Kjellsson built on playful upcycling — secondhand garments deconstructed into sculptural, exaggerated forms; the SS27 presentation 'The Resort' transformed its Copenhagen venue into a beach covered in white sand.
London label founded by Paolina Russo and Lucile Guilmard, blending knitwear craft, technology, suburban nostalgia and sportswear.
Milan-based socio-artistic label founded by designer Galib Gassanoff, rooted in Azerbaijani heritage and artisanal craft; winner of the Zalando Visionary Award 2026.
Danish womenswear label founded by Birgitte and Andrea Herskind, balancing tailoring and fluidity.
Danish womenswear brand founded by Sophia Roe and Charlotte Eskildsen, emphasizing minimalist tailoring, knitwear and longevity.
Copenhagen made-to-order wardrobe by founder Malene Malling, crafted from vintage or limited-stock textiles.
Helsinki-based label founded in 2020 by Alexa Dagmar and Linda Juhola, making elevated, seasonless minimalist staples.

Founded in Copenhagen in 2018 by Oscar Jardorf, O. Files is a character-driven label whose structural design language draws on sartorial tradition, uniform codes and origami-inspired folding; SS27 was its second season on the official CPHFW calendar.

Copenhagen label by creative directors Rikke Baumgarten and Helle Hestehave, known for playful print and pattern play; SS27 asked what happens after the ballet rehearsal, pairing ballet sneakers and tutu-like skirts with daily dressing.

Copenhagen label led by founder Sigurd Bank, focused on cut, fabric and longevity using deadstock, recycled and organic materials; the SS27 collection 'Deadlines' marked 10 years in business with 'overworked' office-wear-inspired silhouettes.
