Copenhagen-based women's label by designer Casey Larkin Blond, rooted in eclectic, individualistic dressing inspired by travel, vintage and real life; the SS27 collection 'Lucky' was the brand's first-ever runway show, marking 13 years since its Copenhagen relaunch.
Fashion and lifestyle brand by Astrid Andersen; 'Stel' means body in Danish, reflecting an inclusive design ethos built around function and longevity.

Nigerian label founded in 2009 by Bubu Ogisi, blending heritage textiles with traditional African craft techniques; winner of the Zalando Visionary Award 2025; the SS27 collection 'Sacred Ecologies' explored cultural displacement through raffia, beads and hand-crafted materials.

Finnish design house founded in 1951, globally renowned for its art of printmaking and bold prints; creative director Rebekka Bay; the SS27 runway show celebrated the art, the artist and the landscape.

Graduate showcase from the Swedish School of Textiles in Borås, Sweden — a standout of over 20 experimental student collections, from embroidered LIDL bags and tops made of hair to LED-light dresses and coats made of tights.

Copenhagen womenswear label by designer Nicklas Skovgaard, founded in 2020, known for narrative-driven collections and innovative fabrication; SS27 dressed 'The Skovgaardettes,' a fictional '60s girl group who emerged from vintage Ford Mustangs in layers of gingham and peplum.

Copenhagen-based clothing label founded in 2022 by Caroline Bille Brahe, rooted in intuition, playfulness and great craftsmanship; expressive, limited-number pieces from the atelier in Borgergade, often using deadstock Chanel, Dries Van Noten and Harris tweed; SS27 'Caro Club' channeled nightlife glamour.

Brazilian label designed by founder and creative director Patricia Bonaldi, in business for about 20 years and in the U.S. for a decade. Known for Brazilian artisan embroidery, fringe, dimensional detailing and draping across beachwear and eveningwear; the collection is manufactured in Brazil. Sold at Saks Fifth Avenue, Bloomingdale’s, Revolve and Bergdorf Goodman. Introduced footwear for fall 2026 and an eyewear collection for spring 2027.
Paris-based label co-founded by designer Danial Aitouganov and stylist Imruh Asha; known for bold color, playful silhouettes and a childlike spirit. 2025 LVMH Prize finalist.
Belgian designer (b. 1965, Liège); launched her eponymous Paris label in 1991 after working as an assistant to Azzedine Alaïa; works from her atelier-showroom at 32 boulevard Ménilmontant, Paris.

One of the most important designers in SPFW history. Since the 1990s, Alexandre Herchcovitch's work has combined technical mastery, alternative-culture references and precise construction, with a rare ability to turn restlessness into clothing; he reclaimed control of his eponymous label via licensing from the InBrands group.

Created by Vivian Rivaben and Silvio de Marchi, Forca Studio works an aesthetic tied to rebellion, São Paulo nightlife and urban subcultures — oversized proportions, high-impact materials and an attitude-loaded image. The brand treats the runway as experience, extending its narrative into set design, casting and performance.

Founded in 1972, the Brazilian jeanswear label helped build the public's relationship with denim as a symbol of youth, attitude and urban life. A subsidiary of the InBrands group, it returns to the SPFW calendar after approximately four years.

The Ceará-based label founded in 2017 by Marina Bitu and Cecília Baima translates Brazilian craft techniques through a contemporary, colorful and experimental language — enlarged fuxicos, pleats, richelieu lace and manually built surfaces — with a strong sustainability value.

shows.venue: Pavilhão das Culturas Brasileiras, Parque Ibirapuera
shows.bio: Transforms urban, sporty and vintage references into fashion with immediate personality — utilitarian pieces, wide proportions, graphic elements and an eye for reuse — converting street codes into runway imagery. Designer and new-business director Alexandre Herchcovitch leads the brand alongside its ÀLG line.

shows.venue: Pavilhão das Culturas Brasileiras, Parque Ibirapuera
shows.bio: Latin America's leading e-commerce marketplace participates as a special project rather than a traditional fashion label. In past seasons it worked with stylist Daniel Ueda's curation to build looks from different decades, trends and products available on the marketplace, connecting content, styling, technology and commerce.

shows.venue: Pavilhão das Culturas Brasileiras, Parque Ibirapuera
shows.bio: Tom Martins made Martins known for a maximalist aesthetic marked by clashing prints, volumes and musical references with an almost performative energy — while also knowing when to strip elements back and work in silence. An unpredictable presence each season.

shows.venue: Pavilhão das Culturas Brasileiras, Parque Ibirapuera
shows.bio: Designer Mayari Jubini brings haute couture, technology and sculptural design together at Artemisi — 3D printing, crystals, rigid structures and futuristic surfaces in a recognizable visual vocabulary that treats the body as a space of experimentation, readable as garment, object and performance.

Designer, artist and professor, Gustavo Silvestre took crochet into a field of experimentation spanning fashion, art and sustainability. His work connects to Projeto Ponto Firme, an initiative promoting education and social transformation through crochet in the prison system, challenging the old separation between craft and high fashion.

shows.venue: Pavilhão das Culturas Brasileiras, Parque Ibirapuera
shows.bio: Founded by Celina Hissa of Ceará, the brand built its trajectory on collaboration with artisan women and the valorization of handcraft knowledge — crochet, bobbin lace, carnauba straw and other Ceará techniques — and became a reference in production transparency, centering the women and communities behind each piece.

shows.venue: Pavilhão das Culturas Brasileiras, Parque Ibirapuera
shows.bio: A partnership between Sou de Algodão, the movement promoting Brazilian cotton, and Ronaldo Fraga, one of the country's most narrative-driven designers. Fraga turns fashion into memory, research and cultural commentary, and the collaboration bridges the production chain, national identity and the imagination of a creator who treats clothing as storytelling.

shows.venue: Pavilhão das Culturas Brasileiras, Parque Ibirapuera
shows.bio: Part of a generation raised mixing fashion, music, internet, games and pop culture. His collections move between East and West, fantasy and urban life, with layering, volumes and characters that seem to belong to their own universes; he has dressed artists including Shakira, Anitta and Gloria Groove, turning the runway into a stage for new imaginaries.

shows.venue: Pavilhão das Culturas Brasileiras, Parque Ibirapuera
shows.bio: João Pimenta turned menswear tailoring into a territory of freedom — skirts, dresses, light fabrics and volumes in dialogue with suits, shirts and classic codes. His work questions gender limits without abandoning technical rigor, with literature, theater and behavior frequently running through his collections.

shows.venue: Pavilhão das Culturas Brasileiras, Parque Ibirapuera
shows.bio: Founded in 2006 by sisters Lilly and Renata Sarti, the brand built a feminine image balancing sensuality, precise design and sophisticated materials — leather, architectural cutouts, prints and shape-shifting pieces that work desire without relying on the obvious.

shows.venue: Pavilhão das Culturas Brasileiras, Parque Ibirapuera
shows.bio: Created by engineer-turned-designer Mônica Sampaio, Santa Resistência celebrates Afro-Brazilian aesthetics and the cultural roots of the Recôncavo Baiano. Prints, fluid dresses, tunics and intense colors appear in a production tied to slow fashion and a more conscious chain, turning ancestry into contemporary presence.

shows.venue: Pavilhão das Culturas Brasileiras, Parque Ibirapuera
shows.bio: One of the names that helped project Brazilian beachwear beyond the country. After the trajectory built with Rosa Chá, Amir Slama develops an eponymous label of cutouts, prints, sensuality and attention to the body; his return to the lineup reinforces a creator who understands beachwear as fashion, behavior and Brazilian identity.

shows.venue: Pavilhão das Culturas Brasileiras, Parque Ibirapuera
shows.bio: The Minas Gerais label under the creative direction of Giovanna Resende works embroidery, transparencies, velvets, cutouts and references to Minas baroque; the 'Doura' collection showed how ancestral techniques can gain sensuality and contemporary reading. It arrives at SPFW after its first fashion-week collection at RioFW in April.

Founded by André Namitala in Rio de Janeiro, Handred developed a light, solar tailoring connected to the Brazilian way of dressing — breathable fabrics, loose silhouettes and artistic references forming a sophisticated fashion without rigidity, keeping uncomplicated elegance as its signature.

After more than a decade away from the calendar, Marcelo Sommer returned to SPFW with Uó, a project dedicated to upcycling and transforming existing garments. The name plays with what was considered outdated, disposable or bad taste; in the designer's hands, treasure-hunting becomes authorial construction.

shows.venue: Pavilhão das Culturas Brasileiras, Parque Ibirapuera
shows.bio: Created by Ana Luisa Fernandes in 2018, Aluf developed a language that brings fashion, art, architecture and sensibility together. Textures, volumes and natural materials appear in constructions that follow the body without losing presence; the brand values artisanal process and treats sustainability as part of creation, not just discourse.

shows.venue: Pavilhão das Culturas Brasileiras, Parque Ibirapuera
shows.bio: Created by stylist Marco Normando and visual artist Emídio Contente, the Amazonian-origin brand uses tailoring, material research and Amazonian references to shift the gaze of Brazilian fashion to the North — working symbols, mythologies and urban contradictions into precisely constructed fashion with territorial identity.

shows.venue: Pavilhão das Culturas Brasileiras, Parque Ibirapuera
shows.bio: A special project dedicated to training and accelerating talent from São Paulo's peripheries. The initiative combines technical instruction, creative development and runway experience, expanding entry possibilities into the market — renewing Brazilian fashion also means opening paths for those historically distant from the big calendars.

shows.venue: Pavilhão das Culturas Brasileiras, Parque Ibirapuera
shows.bio: Founded in Salvador by Hisan Silva and Pedro Batalha, Dendezeiro turned Bahian experiences into an expansive, affective and politically conscious fashion language — colors, volumes, memory, celebration and belonging without reducing Bahia to a tourist image. It returns to SPFW as one of the most vibrant voices of the new Brazilian fashion.

shows.venue: Pavilhão das Culturas Brasileiras, Parque Ibirapuera
shows.bio: Created by Antônio Castro of Alagoas, Foz connects tailoring, craft and Brazilian popular culture. Its collections value techniques and professionals working outside the market's most obvious centers, especially in Alagoas — embroidery, textures and manual constructions with a contemporary finish that never erases the origin of the knowledge used.

shows.venue: Pavilhão das Culturas Brasileiras, Parque Ibirapuera
shows.bio: Debuting at SPFW under the creative direction of Amanda Felisberto, Ammi was created in 2018 and bets on handmade pieces and an idea of luxury built through time, technique and a network of artisans — crochet, transparencies and elaborate surfaces forming a feminine, solar and contemporary image.

shows.venue: Pavilhão das Culturas Brasileiras, Parque Ibirapuera
shows.bio: Founded by Luiz Cláudio Silva, Apartamento 03 emerged in Belo Horizonte and carries in its name the memory of the space where the designer served his first clients. The brand combines technical mastery, tailoring, embroidery and narratives tied to Black identity and the Brazilian experience — precision balanced with emotion.

shows.venue: Dongdaemun Design Plaza (DDP), Art Hall 1, Seoul
shows.bio: Contemporary womenswear combining refined luxury, restrained trends, relaxed elegance, and minimal design.

shows.venue: Dongdaemun Design Plaza (DDP), Art Hall 1, Seoul
shows.bio: Premium Korean womenswear launched in 2011; original graphics reinterpret nature, light, history, art, and culture through an oriental-fantasy lens.

shows.venue: Dongdaemun Design Plaza (DDP), Art Hall 1, Seoul
shows.bio: Duo-founded unisex streetwear label launched in 2017; vivid color, positive storytelling, and borderless styling.

shows.venue: Dongdaemun Design Plaza (DDP), Art Hall 1, Seoul
shows.bio: Eponymous house launched in 1985, known for architectural collections blending Korean tradition, calligraphy, and innovative technique.

Seoul-based womenswear founded in 2017 by sisters Sooy and Jay Park; inspired by the 19th-century British Arts and Crafts movement, with a sustainable-luxury approach combining laser-cutting technology and traditional handcraft.

shows.venue: Dongdaemun Design Plaza (DDP), Art Hall 1, Seoul
shows.bio: Seoul womenswear label founded in 2013, known for refined tailoring, architectural silhouettes, modern femininity, and technology and couture influences.

shows.venue: Dongdaemun Design Plaza (DDP), Art Hall 1, Seoul
shows.bio: Socially and environmentally conscious label associated with upcycling discarded canvases and fabrics, deconstruction, and high-end streetwear.

shows.venue: Dongdaemun Design Plaza (DDP), Art Hall 1, Seoul
shows.bio: Founded in 2014; combines menswear-derived structure with feminine softness and reconstructed tailoring.
Korean unisex label; debuted at Seoul Fashion Week in Spring 2025.

shows.venue: Dongdaemun Design Plaza (DDP), Art Hall 1, Seoul
shows.bio: Tech-couture label founded in 2022, combining AI, robotics, 3D printing, advanced sustainable materials, and traditional craft.

shows.venue: Dongdaemun Design Plaza (DDP), Art Hall 1, Seoul
shows.bio: Founded in 2018; Maison Modern Art Museum translates childlike doodles into wearable art layered over classic, minimalist silhouettes.

shows.venue: Dongdaemun Design Plaza (DDP), Art Hall 1, Seoul
shows.bio: Premium womenswear line of DINT focused on modern women, refined elegance, strength, high-sensitivity fabrics, and delicate silhouettes.

shows.venue: Dongdaemun Design Plaza (DDP), Art Hall 1, Seoul
shows.bio: Korean high-end menswear house launched in 1987, emphasizing tailoring, structural beauty, craft, bright color, and distinctive detail.

shows.venue: Dongdaemun Design Plaza (DDP), Art Hall 1, Seoul
shows.bio: Womenswear label centered on soft, elegant, feminine urban silhouettes with curves, ruffles, trimming, applique, restrained couture detail, and neutral palettes.

shows.venue: Dongdaemun Design Plaza (DDP), Art Hall 1, Seoul
shows.bio: Contemporary lifestyle label launched in 2012, known for bold sculptural proportions, tailoring, and Korean cultural references.

shows.venue: Lotte World Mall World Park, Seoul
shows.bio: Founded in 2009 after the designer spent 15 years at major Korean fashion houses; known for bold prints, saturated color, unconventional silhouettes, and fashion-tech experimentation.

shows.venue: Dongdaemun Design Plaza (DDP), Art Hall 1, Seoul
shows.bio: Unisex contemporary label with genderless formalwear, bold color, and wool and cashmere; Italian-trained tailoring, with the founder having studied at Istituto Marangoni and interned at Moschino.

shows.venue: Dongdaemun Design Plaza (DDP), Art Hall 1, Seoul
shows.bio: Young Seoul label known for monochrome gothic styling, leather, biker references, long black coats, and melancholic runway narratives.

shows.venue: Dongdaemun Design Plaza (DDP), Art Hall 1, Seoul
shows.bio: Womenswear and streetwear label associated with expressive mix-and-match styling, bold color, oversized silhouettes, clashing prints, and mixed textiles.

shows.venue: Dongdaemun Design Plaza (DDP), Art Hall 1, Seoul
shows.bio: Korean menswear label launched in 2005, with a long Seoul Fashion Week history and international showcases.

shows.venue: Lotte World Mall World Park, Seoul
shows.bio: Collective design studio launched in 2019, spanning fashion, architecture, photography, graphics, and content; genderless contemporary streetwear.

shows.venue: Lotte World Mall World Park, Seoul
shows.bio: Young contemporary womenswear with a modern, playful aesthetic and signature blue.

shows.venue: Lotte World Mall World Park, Seoul
shows.bio: Seoul-based menswear label launched in 2004, combining high fashion with a sporty casual aesthetic; known for clean lines, color blocking, and collaborations with Puma, Heineken, Absolut, and MAC.

shows.venue: Lotte World Mall World Park, Seoul
shows.bio: South Korean streetwear brand combining American subculture with an urban edge; bold graphics, striking logos, and relaxed silhouettes. The name combines MAHA, Indonesian for greatness, and GRID, representing checkered pattern.

Shanghai-based clothing brand known for a minimalist, zen-inspired aesthetic rooted in oriental elements and humanism. Its stores and Jiading District headquarters (designed by Yiduan Shanghai, Dezeen, 2018) blend natural materials and unfinished surfaces, extending the brand into a lifestyle concept combining garments, tea, incense, homewares and books.

Qingdao-born designer educated in London: BA in womenswear at the London College of Fashion and MA in womenswear knitwear at the Royal College of Art (2013). Known for experimental, sculptural knitwear in bright colors that offers a witty commentary on the fashion system. Launched her label in 2015; shortlisted for the LVMH Prize that same year; shows at London and Shanghai Fashion Weeks with stockists including Dover Street Market, 10 Corso Como and H-Lorenzo (BoF 500).

Hangzhou-born, Shanghai-based designer who graduated with a BA and MA in Fashion from the Royal Academy of Fine Arts, Antwerp, and launched her eponymous brand in 2018. Known for a modern romantic, maximalist aesthetic of striking color, prints, silk jacquards and intricate embroidery, with asymmetry and experimentation in silhouette; shortlisted for the BOF China Prize and the LVMH Prize, and creator of a Hennessy Chinese New Year 2025 collaboration.
Founded in Shanghai in 2015 by Guan Lin, a Parsons and Donghua University graduate; the womenswear label is known for clean lines and a simple, relaxed approach to modern dressing.
Gomeroi label founded by Colleen Tighe-Johnson that translates commissioned Gomeroi artworks and Dreaming stories into one-off garments, alongside a youth-development social enterprise.

Aboriginal luxury swim and resortwear house founded by Larrakia woman Verity van Ermel Scherer as a tribute to her grandmother, Stolen Generations survivor Valerie “Mattie” van Ermel Scherer; known for silk crêpe kaftans and limited-edition swimwear.
Melbourne-based designer; RMIT graduate who worked with Donna Karan in New York and Cerruti in Paris before launching his label in the late 1990s; known for sculptural couture and ready-to-wear.

Australian made and owned luxury ready-to-wear label founded by Co-Founder and Creative Director Gabriella Pereira; launched at AFW 2021; Sydney-designed and locally made in limited runs, championing masterful tailoring and slow fashion.

shows.venue: Park Hyatt Sydney Boardwalk at The Rocks
shows.bio: Australian fashion house founded by Carla Zampatti in 1965; known for power dressing, precision tailoring and eveningwear.
Sydney swim and resortwear label founded in 2017 by Richard Jarman, inspired by seaside living and the idea of a purposeful pause.
Australian womenswear designer known for fluid draping and precise tailoring.

Contemporary Australian label combining clean lines, languid and sculptural silhouettes, luxury fabrication and a blend of classic and avant-garde influences, spanning unisex ready-to-wear and made-to-order.
Australian fashion house founded in 2008 by Adrian Norris and Edwina Forest, dedicated to raw beauty, tough femininity and effortless cool, bridging coastal and urban dressing.

Sydney-based fashion and textiles designer who launched his eponymous label in 2021; known for emotionally charged garments blurring poetry, digital culture and physical craft, with text-laden prints and sculptural silhouettes; named Emerging Designer of the Year at the 2023 Australian Fashion Laureate.
Contemporary Australian womenswear label founded in 2012.

Label by Sydney designer Hannah Teresa, known for dark romanticism and elevated wardrobe staples; stocked at Reborne Shop, the independent Sydney retail space she also directs. Presented in The Frontier group showcase at AFW 2026.
Label by designer Samantha Diorio, known for sensual, modular, seasonless pieces. Presented in The Frontier group showcase at AFW 2026.
NIDA-trained designer working between fashion and theatre, known for a corsetry-heavy, performance-inflected presentation. Presented in The Frontier group showcase at AFW 2026.
Label by designer Jackie Galleghan, known for quiet restraint and collections honouring craft, storytelling, motherhood and womanhood. Presented in The Frontier group showcase at AFW 2026.

Emerging designer exploring the body through innovative material systems, integrating coding and embroidery; known for 3D-printed twin sets shown at the Melbourne Fashion Festival 2026 National Graduate Showcase. Presented in The Frontier group showcase at AFW 2026.

Designer whose collection ‘Darlings of the Opera Cassette’ drew on an imaginary opera theatre held within a cassette tape, with surreal corsetry manipulated into otherworldly silhouettes. Presented in The Frontier group showcase at AFW 2026.
Slow, consciously created Australian luxury label founded by Charlotte Hicks, built around restraint, quality and longevity, organised as seasonless ‘Editions’.
Byron Bay label founded by Laura May Gibbs with her sister and collaborator Hannah Gibbs, combining art, sustainability and functionality across fashion and activewear.
Australian tailoring and lifestyle label founded by husband-and-wife co-creative directors Joe Farage and Katy Farage.
Label by Dubrovnik-born, Sydney-based designer Karla Špetić, who founded her eponymous line in 2008; known for soft tailoring and a romantic tension between feminine fabrics and sharper silhouettes.
Sydney prêt-à-couture designer known for architectural silhouettes, structured tailoring, fluid drapery and hand embellishment.

shows.venue: Foundation Hall, Museum of Contemporary Art Australia
shows.bio: British-born, Melbourne-based menswear designer; started in men’s footwear before launching a full menswear wardrobe; winner of the 2019 National Designer Award, redefining modern Australian menswear in the space between formal and casual.
Experimental, non-gendered fashion house founded by Jordan Gogos, centred on co-design, upcycling, textile innovation and sculptural wearable art.
Australian luxury womenswear brand established around 2000, known for tactile, natural fabrics and enduring, unconventional design.
Sydney demi-couture label founded in 2014 by Katie-Louise and Lil Nicol-Ford; ethically made to order, working with remnant textiles and queer-history narratives.

Australian concept brand established in 2019, exploring art through pleats and colour; founded by Iuliia Ievdokymenko and Breeana Smith, producing exclusively engineered pleat forms in partnership with one of the world’s oldest pleating factories.

Sydney knitwear designer and UTS Fashion & Textiles graduate who debuted her collection OCEANA — an entirely Shima Seiki-knitted collection inspired by Australia’s marine life — in AFW’s New Gen showcase.
A collaboration between artist Alice Van Meurs and Sarrita King, presented in AFW’s New Gen emerging-designer showcase.

South Sudanese designer behind the label By Gloria Chol; her debut collection ‘Lines of Power’, noted for sculptural silhouettes, dramatic tailoring and elongated denim forms, was featured by Vogue Australia.
First Nations label shown on the Beyond Blak Runway at Melbourne Fashion Festival 2026; selected for AFW’s New Gen emerging-designer showcase.

Contemporary premium un-gendered Australian label founded in 2025; refined minimalism and directional design in small-run production using premium designer deadstock fabrics and local Australian manufacturing; winner of the National Designer Award for Sustainability at Melbourne Fashion Festival 2025.

Sydney-based eponymous label established in 2003; custom made-to-order fine-art collections hand painted by the designer onto ethically sourced eco-cotton, known for masterful drape, intelligent silhouettes and artful colour.

Sustainable First Nations womenswear label founded in 2018 by Wiradjuri entrepreneur Denni Francisco; collaborates with First Nations artists to transpose artworks onto premium-quality garments — Ngali translates to ‘we’ or ‘us’ in several Aboriginal languages.

Sydney-based fashion house by designer Amber Keating, known for streamlined pieces with bold textures — bias-cut dresses, sheer minis and exaggerated blazers — and a rebellious, nonconformist spirit; staged its first runway show in a Potts Point warehouse.

Tokyo-based label launched in 2004 by Yoshio Kubo, who graduated from Philadelphia University's Textile & Science school in 2000, assisted Robert Danes in New York for four years, and returned to Japan in 2004.
Founded in Taiwan in 2017 by Tzu Chin Shen; contemporary womenswear exploring gender, culture, and border-crossing narratives.
Founded in 2025 by Elmo Su; natural materials, quiet beauty, material evolution, and timeless aesthetics.
Established in 2011; Mizuki Ueda launched the label and serves as creative director.
International runway platform committed to curating the future of fashion through diversity and emerging creative voices; the SS27 show featured Nar Rew Ekar, PERRY JONES, and SHINO.
shows.cd: Shoshoni Hostler / Shinobu Uchida / Perry Jones

shows.bio: Partnership presentation by BENCH/ featuring designers Jaggy Glarino, Joey Samson, and Rhett Eala.
shows.cd: Jaggy Glarino / Joey Samson / Rhett Eala

shows.bio: Women's ready-to-wear label established in 1999 by Norio Surikabe, who studied at Kuwasawa Design School and worked in Italy, including at Romeo Gigli and 10 Corso Como's NN Studio.
Established in 2018; Mitsuru Okazaki studied at Ito Garment Research Institute, joined Yohji Design Institute, and worked in pattern production.

Launched in 2016 and rebranded for 2021 A/W as an outerwear-focused label; '360-degree beautiful garments' with functionality, sculptural silhouettes, and an ageless, genderless approach. Meg Miura graduated from ESMOD JAPON and worked under Yoichi Nagasawa.
Established in May 2025 by Eitarou Kamimura, born in Yamaguchi in 2001, recipient of the 97th Soen Award and NEW ENERGY Special Award in June 2023; runway debut September 2025.

Established in 2021; textile-led fashion brand focusing on ways nature has been transformed by human intervention — gardens, botanical gardens, cultivated species — creating imaginary flora and fauna as original textile designs.
Knit brand led by Ryota Murakami, who launched his own brand in 2014; the label changed its name from RYOTAMURAKAMI to pillings in the 2021SS season.

Tokyo label established in 2019, handcrafted in its Tokyo atelier; Yusho Kobayashi graduated from Central Saint Martins after Ritsumeikan University, Tamami Uehara studied textile design at Tama Art University.
Organized by the Taiwan Textile Federation, TAIWAN SELECT is a joint runway presentation showcasing selected Taiwanese fashion brands during Rakuten Fashion Week Tokyo.

Established in 2016 by Tetsuya Doi; unisex label known for constructive forms and dynamic design. Doi graduated from Bunka Fashion Graduate University and studied at coconogacco under Mikio Sakabe and Yoshikazu Yamagata.

Established in 2022, advocating 'Slow Fashion, Slow Luxury' and centering Japanese artisans and craft; Shunsuke Teranishi studied architecture at Kyoto University and worked at Yohji Yamamoto, Carol Christian Poell, Agnona, and Hermès before co-founding MIZEN.
Established in 1955; hat house spanning Akio Hirata OHKO, H.at, and saki et show.
shows.cd: Ohko Hirata / Saki Hirata / Show Hirata

shows.bio: Established in 2019; Taiwan-based brand researching how craft, gestures, and cultural memory remain in materials, including Taiwanese lacquer and Kyoto wax-resist dyeing. SS27 theme 'Becoming,' presented as 'THE ATELIER IS OPEN' — its first-ever Tokyo presentation.
Founded in Taiwan in 1985 by designer Cha-Rin Yeh; the label draws on Taiwanese culture, nature, and lived memory in sharp, gender-neutral urban chic.

Established in 2020 by Sonia Martínez; tailoring, craftsmanship, and construction, revealing hidden garment-making processes. Martínez studied at IED Madrid and worked at Zara, Alexander McQueen, and Phoebe Philo's Céline.

Self-taught French designer based in Paris, born December 1993; known for sculptural hoods, pop-culture, cinema, and video-game references, and signature overlock construction; won the 2026 ANDAM Pierre Bergé Prize.
Established in 2012; Thai craftsmanship, textile experimentation, and geometric silhouettes by designer Wisharawish Akarasantisook.

Established/relaunched in 2025 by Anna Choi; combines Japanese craftsmanship, New York sensibility, European couture techniques, and Korean heritage. Choi previously founded HAENGNAE and works between Tokyo and New York.
Established in 2012 around the concept 'Clothes that will transform you into a HERO for somebody'; opened the flagship store REBLICHAL in Suidobashi in 2017.
Men's and women's ready-to-wear, shoes, bags, and accessories label.

Founded in Tokyo in 2019 by an anonymous design collective; draws on flea-market discovery, folk art, humor, memory, and nostalgia; Tokyo Fashion Award 2023 recipient and LVMH Prize 2024 semifinalist. The SS27 show was presented through Rakuten's 'by R' support project.

Launched in 2018 by Tsukasa Kudo; prioritizes comfort, silhouettes, and clothing grounded in everyday life. Kudo studied at the Royal Academy of Fine Arts Antwerp and worked at Jacquemus, JW Anderson, and Y/Project.
